# Welcome to the Code of Ethics

The Code of Ethics (often abbreviated to CoE) is a ruleset written and maintained by the Thunder Scientific Corporation Ethics Committee. It serves as the base rules and as a standard to uphold for all personnel in the Corporation.
To ensure a lack of bias and fair punishment, **all personnel, with the sole exception of the Administrator, are subject to the Code of Ethics at all times, unless in terms which apply to their job.**

The Code was created by the Ethics Committee to ensure the Corporation would not fall into chaos and distrust despite the challenging and uncertain circumstances it survives in. TSC must remain strong, for humanity's sake.

The purpose of this section is to serve as information regarding the combatant status of TSC personnel when they are deployed on a certain department, as well as the combatant status of GoI members when they are operating on-site. This is a general basis which departments go off from, they can stray away from it but must stay reasonable for their changes.

The following sections will explain all positions which personnel are assigned when deployed on a specific team or department. Any exceptions for subdivisions (like the Technical Task Squad) will be listed and explained in detail in this section as well.

**Combatant**

All personnel which possess the status of being a combatant are site security personnel and are expected to respond to any and all threats on-site to protect civil personnel. They may engage hostiles freely as long as the criteria is met to do so.

The following list of departments, Groups of Interest are deemed Combatant:

- Security Department
- Combat Medics
- Technical Task Squad are considered full combatants but may only act as such in S1 and CTZ. Additionally, TTS may act as full combatants in S2 under the conditions listed within their handbook: [https://trello.com/c/nmYUka9k/65-1-4-sector-permissions](https://trello.com/c/nmYUka9k/65-1-4-sector-permissions "smartCard-inline")
- Security Engineering Team (SET)
- Recontainment Unit (Asset Handlers)
- RAH (Assets)
- Special Operations
- Juggernaut Unit

**Semi-Combatant**

All personnel which possess the status of being a Semi-Combative are defensive personnel which only engage hostiles in protection of others and themselves. This status is mostly given to intelligence personnel.

While Semi-Combatants are to stay defensive, if a situation gets out of hand and the site is deemed in high danger (Code RED+ and specified scenarios in the respective entity with EC approval) they may elevate to combatant status to assist combatants.

Semi-Combatants follow the same regulations in engagement with hostiles outside of their combatant status, however they may chase down any hostile which poses a threat and/or engaged with them to terminate them.

Semi-Combatants may freely terminate disguised personnel for the duty of internal security on-site.

The following list of departments, Groups of Interest are deemed Semi-Combatants:

- Internal Security Bureau
  - ISB have their own written regulations regarding their combatant status. This can be found on their Master Guidelines.
- Ethics Committee Rogue Response
- Highway Patrol

Semi-combatants may not participate in hostile raids. (Unless the department/division has gotten permission from the hostile group to engage in raids.)

**Non-Combatant**

All personnel which possess the status of being a non-combatant are civil personnel which may only engage hostiles for self-defense of themselves or other non-combatant personnel as stated in section B3 of the Code of Ethics.

The following list of departments, Groups of Interest are deemed non-combatant:

- Research & Studies
- Medical Department
- Utility & Maintenance
- RAH Assets are an extension of RECON and work together with assigned handlers to deal with breaches and protection of CTZ. The default state of assets is to be non-combative in CTZ and only attack hostiles if they enter specimen chambers or are engaged by hostiles. If an Asset is paired with a handler, they gain full combative status.
- Utility & Maintenance Specialized Branch
- External Relations
- Ethics Committee
- Facility Personnel
- Administrative Department
- Manufacturing Department teams (Site Engineer, Quality Assurance, etc.)

Hostile Groups of Interest may go on peacekeeping to become neutral with TSC for a certain amount of time. Whenever peacekeeping is in effect, their units are to follow the Code of Ethics and refer to this page for information regarding their on-site combatant status. Hostile GoI units which can go on peacekeeping are marked with a * at the end of the unit's name. Hostile GoI members who are deployed to bodyguard non-combatant members of their own GoI are assigned semi-combatant status. For the time they are deployed on-site, they are to follow the Code of Ethics and to be considered non-hostile.

All corporation personnel are expected to treat anyone with due respect at all times. All individuals, human, post-human, and deceased must be treated with a certain level of respect that one would expect others to owe them.

Certain behaviors are required to include the following:

- Personnel may not harass other individuals by [Roblox's Terms of Service,](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846-Roblox-Terms-of-Use "‌") these are defined by repeated actions that meet the listed criteria as violating Roblox's Terms of Service.
- Personnel must refrain from insulting or slandering individuals or groups by Roblox's Terms of Service
- Personnel must not discriminate against individuals based on religion, gender, race, sexual orientation, disability, national origin, or any other protected personal identifying information by Roblox terms of service.
- Personnel are expected to follow the [Roblox Community Guidelines](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/203313410-Roblox-Community-Standards "‌") and breaches of such guidelines are liable for infractions in addition to moderator actions.
- Personnel must show respect to the corpses of the deceased by not defiling or disrespecting the body of the deceased.
- Personnel should not participate in behavior that may be disruptive to other personnel's departmental duties.

Additional rules also apply to ensure the Corporation's site remains respectable, clean, and professional at all times for all individuals involved.

- Personnel should not hold long arguments or sensitive conversations in populated areas especially when it disrupts gameplay or site events.
- Personnel should avoid playing loud, irritating, or inappropriate/bypassed audio. You can play semi-loud music with the radio, but if the audio is too loud you should not play it.
- Personnel should take care to respect the personal space of others by not climbing, mounting, entering, or coming uncomfortably close to any person after being told to stop.

English is recommended as the official language for personnel on site and are liable to any difficulties of communication should any other language be used.

All personnel have at their disposal a handheld radio which can be used to effectively communicate with other personnel across the facility.

Due to these portable radios being very valuable for communication, they have a set of rules when it come to using them to ensure they are used effectively.

When using radios, you are expected to follow all behavioral, in-game, and Roblox ToS rules as with standard communication.

Radios also have their own set of additional rules:

- You may not spam the radios with unnecessary messages
- You may not use the ping feature ( ex. \@‌everyone ) for unnecessary messages. This is reserved for important messages only.
  - How the ping feature works is if you very specifically type out a teams name, it makes your text yellow for them and provides an alert noise. Example: “ \@‌Recontainment Unit There is a breach in S2 “ would be yellow for RECON, allowing them to see it easier.
- You may not provide misinformation or lies on the radio, if you are unsure about something make sure to state so.

There are also certain channels available for certain departments. You may only use said channels for their designed purpose.

Combative channels are to speak about emergencies, callouts, site state, etc… without non-combative personnel seeing the messages. Make sure any important site security operations are done on these channels so that it remains focused.

Staff channels are there to communicate with each other about their duties on site and is typically reserved for coordinating site events.

The Global channel is a channel where you can speak freely about anything.

**IF THE RADIOS ARE BROKEN AND CHANNELS DON’T WORK PROPERLY, YOU MAY IGNORE THE PART ABOVE.**

Personnel may not enter areas their security clearance does not permit them for, unless escorted by an authorized individual with valid reasoning. Some areas, which are usually marked, may have more specific requirements for when personnel are permitted to enter them. These areas are the following:

### Unit 4

Unit 4 of the CTZ is a checkpoint that personnel whitelisted by JU may only enter inside with valid reasoning. Anyone who is within the U4 checkpoint or containment without proper authorization may be terminated or cuffed out at the discretion of JU operatives.

The following personnel may enter the Unit 4 checkpoint:

- ISB
- AD Administrative Intern+
- SD Department Secretary+
- SO
- JU Captain+ on any allied team.
- EC Board Member+ only when spectating a U4 test.

These personnel may freely roam the checkpoint. Any personnel who disrupt the operation of the checkpoint may be forced out of the checkpoint at the discretion of the personnel operating the checkpoint. JU operatives may order these personnel away from the area if they want to.

The following personnel are whitelisted to enter Unit 4 but need valid reasoning to enter the checkpoint:

- RECON Junior Operative+ when conducting duties.
- RSD Specialists Beginner Specialist+ when hosting or spectating Unit 4 tests.
- Level-5+ Personnel that are not on the Facility Personnel team.
- SET (Specialist Architect+) May guard the U4 checkpoint following their internal regulations
- RAH MR+ may guard the U4 checkpoint whilst paired, following their internal regulations

In addition to the list above, the Juggernaut Unit have a public spread-sheet to keep track individual whitelists/blacklists along with specifics regarding groups' permissions within Unit 4.
[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PaayMCiBx73YBqZtWiffUvHeDtlzoaBryQGR_utiU_w/edit?gid=0#gid=0](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PaayMCiBx73YBqZtWiffUvHeDtlzoaBryQGR_utiU_w/edit?gid=0#gid=0 "smartCard-inline")
If a user is listed under the “Blacklisted” roster, they are not to enter U4 or else they can be met with a B1 infraction for violating their blacklist.

Group of Interests are blacklisted from entering Unit 4 entirely and may only enter with the authorization of a JU Lieutenant.

RAH assets are blacklisted from entry by default, and may only enter briefly for sweeping if they have a Handler that they are paired with. They may not enter regardless if there is a suspected or confirmed breach of Specimen 239. Handlers may enter under the same regulation as standard RECON.

Special Operations may go on the U4 checkpoint to deal with hostiles if there are no other specialized forces responding.

JU Operatives may authorize combatant personnel into Unit 4 following their internal regulations. Special Operations Corporal+ may also authorize combatives into Unit 4 for valid reasons, however JU may override this anytime.

‌

### Central Facility Mainframe (CFM)

The CFM is heavily restricted, and guarded by Special Operation or Juggernaut Unit members. Any personnel found within the CFM, that has not had authorization, is allowed to be killed on-sight.

Whitelisted personnel:

- ISB
- AD Administrative Intern+
- SD Department Secretary+
- SO
- JU Captain+ on any allied team.
- Recontainment unit may freely access CFM up to the checkpoint (second garage door)
- SET (Specialist Architect+) may also access CFM up to the checkpoint in order to grab building props for fortifying the U4 checkpoint, they may not loiter

If the tamper protection has sent out an alert, or the CFM flag has been captured, only whitelisted and the following combatives may respond;

- Recontainment Unit
- Security Department SHR+

Juggernaut Unit’s Operator+ may authorize any other combatives into the CFM if there has been a triggered heist or a flag has been capped. In the event of a radiation breach within the CFM, TTS (Fumigator+) are permitted to enter up to outer CFM (includes bridge).
Additionally, SD SHR+ may authorize other combatives into CFM if JU or SO do not respond within **10 minutes** to heists or flag captures.

If there has **not** been a trigger and hostiles are present, only whitelisted combatives are allowed to handle it. During that time, members of Special Operations and Juggernaut Unit are allowed to authorize other combatives into the CFM to assist.

Groups of Interest may not enter the CFM unless authorized by JU or they are a part of the list of whitelisted combatives and the requirement for entry is met.

While there are no hostiles, JU have the highest authority within the CFM. If no JU are present, SO will take precedence. (and if neither, ISB)
Even during times of no hostile activity, the CFM should **not** be opened randomly; only if there is a suspected hostile inside.

‌

### Warhead Silo

The checkpoint at the Warhead Silo is a heavily restricted area controlled by Special Operations members. Any personnel that are not authorized to enter the area are to be killed on-sight.

The following personnel are whitelisted and may freely enter:

- SO
- SO Field Chief+ on any allied team
- ISB
- AD Administrative Intern+
- JU Operative+

The following personnel may enter during specific events that occur inside the Silo:

- RECON/RAH during specimen breaches
- TTS during rad breaches
- All combatives during code delta

If hostiles are present during all codes except delta, after 5 minutes of no JU/SO response (5 minutes after being pinged/notified) All combatives may enter to clear out hostiles, they are to leave afterwards.

Additionally, when performing Code Ambers, all AD personnel can enter the silo with Special Operations escort.

### Surface

The surface, an irradiated yet restricted area patrolled, guarded, and overseen by Special Operations members.
Personnel of L3+ may only go outside the facility with valid reasoning, unless you are one of the following:

- TTS running a “Rad Run” or dealing with radiation on the surface
- TTS dealing with CIS or specimen breaches
- All HWY-P & Rangers
- RECON/RAH dealing with CIS or specimen breaches
- RSD personnel during tests
- VP personnel during a CIS rehabilitation event
- PB personnel during therapy related events
- Any combative during the escorting of an event
- All personnel when there is an active Code Delta or Code Amber drill
- AD Administrative Intern+
- Any Intelligence Personnel

External Relations members are allowed to bring non-TSC staff into the site under supervision.

When opening the surface gate you must say so on the radio, accompanied by an \@‌Combatives ping. Always close the gate when you are finished to avoid any escapees.
When the gate is opened, remember to grab your keycard back; failure to do so will result in punishment.

SO has the highest authority within the TSC side of the surface and can order anyone back into the facility and or kill trespassers within the designated TSC areas. Failure to comply with them allows for you to be killed on-sight.

Additionally, SO may not terminate personnel who are doing their duties whilst on the surface. SO HR+ may override usage of the surface gate in the event of an emergency when ultimately necessary.

If you are unaware of where the TSC side of the surface is; see the image listed at the bottom.

---

### No CoE Zone / Slums

The slums, also notoriously known as the "No CoE Zone", are located within Sector 1 of the facility. The Sub-level 6 Hall B staircase located between the No CoE Zone and the Sector 1 Panic Shelter is not to be considered part of the No CoE Zone.

All rules of the Code of Ethics except A1, A2, F1, and B4 regarding radios and F2 are voided within the zone. Handbook regulations and contract regulations still apply in this zone unless said otherwise by the respective division, department, or GoI. All hostile groups that are authorized to be in Maxiburger during non-raid times may also enter this area and participate in it.

The area covers:

- “ gooberbean’s wafflehouse “
- Sewers
- Slums behind Maxiburger
- Maxiburger
  - While in the area of Maxiburger, you are not to disrupt duties of other departments, including Maxi itself (i.e. messing with their equipment, pulling lockdown and light switches, etc.), on purpose (if severe enough, may lead to an F2 infraction alongside a global blacklist)
  - You must treat others with respect and not engage in combat with Maxi staff without valid reasoning (i.e. Maxi staff violating their own handbook, abusing their power / attacking you without a proper reason)
  - You are not to mass-murder people within the area (i.e. any act which results in large amount of casualties)
  - You are not to intentionally act provocatively towards anyone, rules regarding harassment still apply and will be enforced.
  - Maxiburger employees are not permitted to leave Maxiburger grounds unless participating in Maxiburger events such as Maxi-Train, Free-Range Employees, or a rally/patrol. They may also leave if H10 is active, they are delivering food, they have authorization from Manager+ or AD, or if they are a KIP with escorts.
  - Maxiburger employees are treated as FP outside of Maxiburger, requiring them to follow the CoE.

**Note:** Any side regulations, alongside hostile termination procedures on Maxiburger territory are to be discussed between Maxi and department commands.

You may find Maxiburger handbook here: [https://trello.com/b/6QuAt0F8/tsc-maxiburger-handbook-new](https://trello.com/b/6QuAt0F8/tsc-maxiburger-handbook-new "smartCard-inline")

You may not shoot personnel outside of the No CoE zone while being in the said zone and vice versa.

You may not harm intelligence personnel (EC, ISB) inside the No CoE zone.

---

Non-combatant personnel whose special clearance allows them to enter routes marked for combatant personnel may enter them at their discretion. Some areas may require non-combatant personnel to be accompanied by security forces, and the required degree of protection may vary.

Personnel may not enter any hostile spawns unless there are confirmed hostile TS in the spawn. Personnel may not use any routes which are designated to be used by raiders, these include vents, teleports, doors, etc.

If personnel have an upgraded clearance from another department, they may utilize it as long as it doesn’t overstep the authority of the team they are on.

# Site-Wide Emergency Protocols

In the event of a site-wide emergency, the correct site code color should be activated so the proper announcement be made over the PA system that matches the situation.
Codes do not need to be raised or lowered in order nor does there need to be a set amount of time before lowering the code. (Code can be changed from Gamma down to Blue if there is no more reason for Red or Gamma)

The following Emergency Code Levels currently exist in-game:

**Code Green:**

This is the standard color code for site operations when there are no recognized threats against site stability. When there aren't any threats that pose a danger to site stability, code green should be reinstated and site operations should be continued as normal.

**Code Blue:**

A potential threat is roaming the site with a high probability of posing a threat to site stability. All personnel should have heightened awareness of any possible threats around them, and report them when they are spotted. This status should be set if any of the following conditions apply:

- Armed hostiles were reported to be within the facility
- Contained Infected Subjects are confirmed to be missing from their containment zone
- Large groups of escaped inmates roaming the facility

**Code Red:**

A confirmed threat is roaming the site and is an active threat to site stability. Any non-combatant personnel are advised to vacate the current sector the threat is in, and to make their way to a designated safe area. Security forces may order non-combatants into a safe area if deemed necessary. This status should be set if any of the following conditions apply:

- There is an armed group of hostiles reported on-site actively contributing to site instability
- There is a confirmed Infected outside of the Containment Zone
- Any amount of radiation has breached containment
- A rogue staff member has been reported within the facility

‌

**Code Gamma:**

A highly dangerous threat has been detected in multiple sectors of the facility, and is actively contributing to site instability. No non-combatants may be outside of the nearest designated safe area/panic shelter with an exception of medical personnel in accordance to C1. This status should be set by L-4+ personnel if any of the following conditions apply:

- Any U4 specimen has breached their containment chamber.
  - The “containment chamber” is the room at which the specimen spores reside.
- A large number of hostiles are actively contributing to site instability and normal security forces cannot handle the threat
- A large amount of staff have reported to have gone rogue
- Code Red has been on for a **constant** 40 minutes+ without any sign of the threat(s) causing it being resolved.
  - SD Warrant Officer+ can authorize gamma after code red has been on for a constant 30 minutes

RECON, SO, and JU may set gamma if one of the requirements above are met. (Even if they are not L4+)

Codes past **Code Gamma+** are only to be activated by L5+ Personnel.

**Code Epsilon:**

Full site control has been lost to hostile forces. Any means to get to a designated safe area is permitted even if that means bypassing Code of Ethics rulings based on clearance or self-defense. This status should be set if any of the following conditions apply:

- Most sectors of the facility have been overrun by hostiles
- A full site breach or riot has occurred where no area in the site is considered safe

**Code Delta:**

The situation on site is beyond repair, and the on-site nuclear armaments have been primed to detonate and destroy anything inside the facility. All personnel must evacuate to the surface by any means necessary and security forces should help personnel evacuate and prevent hostiles from escaping to the surface.

The on-site nuclear armaments may only be activated by personnel who possess an administrative clearance (AD+) or SO/SD 2iC+ during the event of when site control cannot be regained after a Code Epsilon has been initiated after at least 20+ minutes. The nuclear warhead detonation is only to be used as a last resort, and may only be activated if the following applies:

- Site control cannot be regained during a **Code Epsilon** after 20+ minutes
- The entire site is compromised, and a member of the Administrative Department gives authorization for a **Code Delta** to be initiated.

If the onsite contingency system is activated without an evacuation announcement, then it is assumed to be compromised by hostile forces and emergency evacuation is to commence unless Security Forces regain control and deactivate the system.

**Code Amber:**

A simulation of the evacuation protocol performed during a **Code Delta** event that is used as a drill to ensure that all personnel present know what to do when an evacuation is called, and should be considered with the same urgency and efficiency for an actual **Code Delta** event.

- A **Code Amber** may only occur with the permission of a member of the Administrative Department and is to be supervised by Security and/or Divisional Command staff
- Before a **Code Amber** is declared, all on-site personnel are to be warned for at least 5 minutes to ensure that any ongoing events are canceled, concluded, or postponed.
- **Code Amber** should only be called up to 2 times per month and should last a maximum of 15 minutes.

A designated safe area is any one of the following:

- A breach or panic shelter.
- A department office that isn't easily accessible to hostile forces.
- Any area designated by present security forces on-site to be considered safe and defend-able from hostile forces as an alternative.
- TSCZ Control Room, Main Control Room in SD U2, and the CISCZ Control room

Personnel should remain in their safe location for the duration of the emergency unless they are:

- Requested and escorted by a combatant for instances of **Code Red** emergencies.
- Forced out of the safe area by hostile forces.
- **Code Delta** has been activated and an evacuation commences.

Weapons ranging from light batons to heavy assault rifles are all part of the arsenal of certain divisions for various reasons. To ensure these arms are used appropriately, certain restrictions apply.

- You may not break or damage important breakable objects. (Drones, pipes and their valves etc.) without reason with any weapon. The acceptable reasons to destroy breakable objects are if hostiles must be terminated behind them, hostiles control the equipment or you are trying to gain quicker access through a route.
- Only buildings that completely prevent access to areas of the facility may be destroyed. Additionally structures that are not being actively used/serve no purpose that clutter hallways and rooms may be destroyed. (_Refer to D1 for specifications about TS builds in TSCZ_).
- Innocent individuals may not be injured with any weapon.
  - The exception(s) to this is if you are in the kill zone of Internal Security Bureau members or Juggernaut Unit Operatives, or if you are a Security Department member following the personal space clause found within their handbook. A baseline of these regulations follow a 5-stud stun (SD) or kill zone (ISB, JU) if they violate the personal space of the individual. There may be instances where they can terminate you for intervening with their duties after receiving a warning from them.
  - Personnel who carry it may use the blood transfusion gun to take blood from subjects inside of solitary confinement.
  - Combat Medics may use stims on personnel with their own internal regulations of consent or free-use
  - Special Operations Operatives may terminate individuals for violating their personal space following A1.
    - This being about 3 studs or on their characters head, hugging them, etc.

---

Non-combatant personnel follow additional regulations to these rules:

- Non-combatant personnel may not carry large or automatic weaponry unless given special authorization from the Administrative Department (Administrative Intern+ or through an executive order such as H10 when active.)
- Non-combatants may not harm hostiles or use weapons unless they are doing so in self-defense or are protecting other defenseless personnel (Downed combatants, unarmed non-combatant personnel…) from being attacked or threatened with harm.
  - Note that your priority should be escaping the threat if there is a safe way to do so. You may not constantly defend others or run after someone to finish them off since your duty is to escape the danger.
  - If you have downed a hostile in self-defense in an appropriate way, you are permitted to finish them off.
- Non-combatants may fire upon hostiles that have taken control over a vehicle that belongs to them and chase the hostile in order to retrieve it. If you have downed the hostile in the process of it, you are allowed to finish them off.
- Non-combatants may not take any weaponry that is unavailable for them to use in their firearm permit. They are only allowed to use weapons available to them when they spawn or in their department headquarters unless stated otherwise by their departmental command (L5+).
- Additionally, when on the Facility Personnel team you may only use weapons if you have an issued firearm permit.
- In the case that you are a Contained Infected Personnel (CIP) with over 200  Health, you may not wield any firearms exept for the TASER. Note that you must have a Type-A Firearm permit to use the TASER.

The regulations for firearm permits regarding personnel can be found here:

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gccqesU3vb94henWzNkBQA3MSR8OmxYqkgETIuc-JF0/edit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1gccqesU3vb94henWzNkBQA3MSR8OmxYqkgETIuc-JF0/edit "smartCard-inline")

---

Personnel who receive / purchase unauthorized weaponry. Any black market item, items from John Recycle, or weaponry from hostile forces that is not normally available to you in your standard loadout, may not use it and should surrender it to a combatant or administrator, or they should dispose of it as soon as possible.

Combatants cannot use weapons surrendered to them or weapons they have picked up unless they have access to them normally or are authorized to use them.

‌

---

### Manual turret

The manual turret can be purchased from the SDHQ garage, it is only to be used by full combatives, additionally these rules must be followed:

- No more than 2 turret mays be welded to any 1 vehicle.
- Turrets may not be taken into spawn areas (TSCZ, CISCZ, SDHQ, etc.)
  - The exception to this is in TSCZ, where up to 2 turrets may be placed in inner TSCZ behind the red line.
- Turrets are not to be left lying around unattended as hostiles can take them.
- Semi combatives may use the turrets on Red+.
cards.name: Rule B3 | Weapon Handling

cards.desc:
Tools ranging from wands, cuffs, etc. are all part of loadouts for certain personnel. To ensure these tools are used appropriately, certain restrictions apply.

### Cuffs

Personnel may use cuffs for certain reasons, whether it be on inmates or other personnel. When they do use them, the following restrictions apply.

Personnel may not do the following actions on cuffed individuals:

- Threaten to drop the individual over harmful or deadly ledges
- Infect/ Have others infect the cuffed/carried individual unless in a test
- Give contraband to the individual
- Kill or intentionally harm the cuffed/carried individual, unless:
  - The cuffed/carried individual is an inmate that is being brought to solitary confinement or a test/event and they must be stunned to avoid risks of escape before putting them in Solitary Confinement, or a large weapon is found on them and they must be terminated.
  - The cuffed/carried individual is an inmate undergoing a test and the test requires it to minimize collateral damage while disposing of the Test Subject. This also applies to any inmates who misbehave during a test and need to be terminated.
  - The cuffed individual is an inmate who is actively using other people as cover after attacking personnel.
  - The cuffed individual is wearing any disguise regardless if no contraband is possessed.
  - The carried individual is an armed inmate who has been downed in the TSCZ and was taken to a safer location to finish them off to ensure minimal collateral damage and the securing of the subject's weapons.

Inmates who were found glitching may be cuffed, but it is recommended you report these actions to the in-game moderation team and leave it to them. Additionally, you’re permitted to cuff exploiters as long as you have evidence of them exploiting, but you must be careful not to restrain moderators under this clause.

Infected specimens may not be cuffed unless the said infected is one of the following:

- An unarmed CIS.
- An infected within the CIS-CZ.
- Being brought back from/during an event with the host's permission. Detainment rules from the section above apply whilst they are cuffed.
- An Armed CIS may be cuffed if:
  - The CIS is in or walking away from a restricted area.
  - The CIS is walking away from an open BM vent.
  - The CIS was seen out of containment but has returned to containment.
  - The CIS is seen binning, wielding, dropping, or has contraband visibly.
  - The CIS is near another CIS who has dropped contraband.
  - Additionally, combatives must attempt to allow them to willingly drop their weapons before apprehending them.
  - Combatives may cuff and wand CIS if they have reasonable suspicion of them carrying any concealed weaponry.
- CIS that use the '/e surrender' emote upon being confronted may be cuffed regardless of weapons or contraband.

Personnel may only be cuffed/carried when:

- They have been downed and must be relocated to a safe area to revive them.
- They have gone rogue.
- You are a part of EC or ISB.
- Said personnel are your subordinates in your current department.
- You have received explicit permission from a DI+ of the department member you’re cuffing.
- You have received permission from the person you're cuffing.

You may not use your cuffs pointlessly or disruptively whether it’s an inmate or personnel that you’re restraining.

---

### Wand

The wand is a tool that is typically part of the arsenal of combatant personnel or intelligence personnel to check if inmates and/or personnel are in any possession of contraband. You must not use the wand pointlessly or disruptively and follow the listed regulations while using it:

- Checking inmates for contraband if they are acting suspiciously. (Covering up their back constantly, having been near a TS who had contraband, avoiding security presence, etc…)
- Wanding other personnel for testing purposes.
- Checking inmates for contraband freely if the respective protocol is active in your department. (Including SD contraband sweep drill.)
- Confiscating any type of contraband including lethal drinks when they are being brought to solitary confinement.
- Checking personnel for unauthorized firearms or to verify their identity.

Do not use the wand to obtain undroppable items (such as special keycards, tools, weapons, etc.), or to deliberately drop every single item from one's inventory.

---

### Grenades

Throwables can be vital for support in active combat. To ensure they do not get misused and for the safety of other personnel, the following regulations should be followed when using throwables:

- Utility Grenades (Flashbangs, Smoke Grenades) should not be randomly or disruptively used.
- Harmful throwables (e.g. grenades, explosives) should not be randomly deployed intentionally.
- Frag Grenades should only be used if the EOP is Code Red+ or higher.
- Sterilizers should not be randomly or disruptively used and also should not be used in combination with any form of fire unless authorized or there is no clear and present danger to surrounding personnel.

---

### Radio

The radio is a vital communication tool available for all personnel to freely use. When using a radio, the user is expected to follow all behavioral, in-game and Roblox ToS rules as with standard communication.

Radios also possess their own set of additional rules:

- Radios may not be used for irrelevant communication during emergencies or during exchange of important information.
- You may not provide misinformation or lies on the radio, if you are unsure about something make sure to state so.
- You may not use the ping feature ( ex. \@‌everyone ) for unnecessary messages. This is reserved for important messages only.

The ping feature of the radio is similar in nature to the one on Discord, simply type in a users or teams name after a “ \@ “ and the user/team will be pinged alongside your message. You may also use \@‌Combatives to ping all combatants and \@‌everyone to ping everyone which possesses a radio.

#### Channels

The radio has a few channels in its disposition, each channel having a different purpose.

- Global channels may be used freely by anyone for any reason.
- Staff channels are reserved for staff/event coordination.
- Combatant channels are reserved for callouts, emergencies and other site security topics (like SC strikes)
- _The existence of any other channel is a myth._

---

### Pagers & CSM Terminals

Communication & Shift Manager terminals are another way to establish communication between personnel alongside radios, they also come with a pager. Any message transmitted from the CSM terminal is received by personnel's pager within a 200 meters radius of said terminal.

Pagers and CSM terminals follow a set of rules that is nearly identical to the rules of radio usage. You must follow behavioral rules and don't be disruptive.

---

### Medical equipment

Medical equipment (Splint, Tourniquets, etc) is found in various locations where medical personnel work or are commonly found. The equipment is generally restricted for use by personnel who are not designated medical staff. The rules are as follows:

- Personnel may not possess medical equipment.
- Personnel are required to dispose of or hand over medical equipment to the nearest medical personnel.
- Personnel may use medical equipment as necessary only when no MDs are available nearby, otherwise, they must resort to being treated by the medical personnel or the medical staff NPCs.
- Disinfectants may be carried and used in the case of an emergency by personnel at risk of infection.

---

### Miscellaneous

Personnel are prohibited from intentionally destroying their departmental or GOI-issued non-weapon equipment in any manner. (examples: ID papers, Cuffs, Keycards, Radio, etc.)
cards.name: Rule B4 | Tool Usage

cards.desc:
#### PA System

The global PA system is only to be used to send server-wide announcements by L4+ personnel, GoI Command members or by Special Operations MRs regarding any lock down procedure.
Additionally, whilst using the PA you are required to speak in a professional and appropriate manner.
You may only use the PA system to announce the following:

- The start of a raid, breach, riot and/or lock down.
- Ordering non combative personnel to a designated safe area when the proper codes are applied
- Declaring a site evacuation during a Code Delta or Code Amber
- High ranking combative personnel ordering their subordinates
- MD High ranks announcing the start of a Scenario Event
- JU members announcing a JU designation
- Combatives may announce when the PA gets retaken from a hostile force, professionalism rules must still be followed.
- Psychology Branch may use the PA to announce hosted events such as group therapy.
- Research and Studies personnel may use the PA to request for assisting users (other RSD, combatives, etc.) for testing purposes.
  - People who utilize the PA for this reason must be sure to send a clear and to the point message.

‌

Combatives, regardless of rank, must use the PA to announce the start and end of a sectoral lockdown, including CTZ lockdowns.

#### TSCZ local PA

The local PA in the TSCZ may not be used disruptively and is to be used for announcing non-combative events.
It may also be used to announce TSCZ lockdowns instead of the global PA.

---

#### TSCZ Lockdown

In the event of a threat/incident affecting the Test Subject Containment Zone, the lock down of the TSCZ may be used in various ways and may only be used for the following reasons:

- A breached specimen is inside the TSCZ or ventilation systems connected to it, and it has not been contained for 20 minutes. If the specimen is actively causing a mass infection in the TSCZ it may be turned on.
- Any amount of radiation has breached containment and is creating a risk of harming Test Subjects or Personnel.
- A large amount of inmates have been constantly rioting for 5+ during Code Gamma+, which cannot be handled by normal security forces.
- TSCZ has been overrun by Hostile GOI's for 5 minutes.
- A large number of hostiles are causing a disruption within the ventilation system, and a Security Force (full combative) HR+, GoI Command Member, or Special Operations MR authorizes a ventilation sweep. Before initiating a lock down, you must warn inmates via the PA system prior to activating it.
- It has been Code Red for 45+ minutes, or Code Gamma for 5+ minutes

The TSCZ Riot Gate, can be engaged by anyone under these circumstances:

- TSCZ is unguarded or taken over.
  - Can also be used if understaffed (less then 2 combatives)
- Code Red+.
- Mass infection is happening in TSCZ during a breach.
- A system riot is occurring.
- RSD is starting any kind of test
  - The Riot Gate must be opened after the briefing room is cleared

---

#### Ventilation

A set of universal rules for who can enter into any ventilation;

- Juggernaut Units whenever they deem necessary.
- Special Operations during on-going system riots, raids as well as breaches and lock downs, or when armed inmates are using the ventilation shafts as cover.
  - “Using as cover” would be if an inmate is actively showing hostility and running to the vents for safety.
- Combatant units entering the ventilation shaft to finish off a downed hostile that they were previously chasing. You must immediately leave after doing so.

##### **TSCZ Black market/vents**

Vents that are connected to the TSCZ black market may be accessed during these conditions along with previously stated;

- Fumigators or Combatives with partial/full immunity during a confirmed breach within the area, to sweep for any potential or confirmed biohazards.
  - Immunes that enter the Black market without an authorized vent sweep, during a breach under this rule, may ONLY engage in combat with _infected subjects_ and not anyone else outside of the Self Defense clause.
- Combative units during TSCZ lockdowns that are **not** caused by a breach.
- TSC based Security force (Security Department, RECON, SET, etc.) in groups of 2, when armed inmates are using the ventilation shafts as cover when there are no Special Operations present.

Exhaust vent below the TSCZ Black-market is considered NOT connected to the Black-market, when the BM LD is off.
When the BM LD is on, exhaust is then considered “connected to BM”.
Stacking to get into the BM, or to get a shot into the BM vent, is not allowed. (Unless one of the requirements is met for you to be allowed within the BM ventilation.)

##### **Additional Black Market Vents**

Other black market vents such as "Liams" (Sector 2 black market above Sector 2 commons), the vending machine market, and surface black market, all follow the non-TSCZ specific rules in the points above. However, additional conditions apply for _**these areas specifically**_ such as;

- Special operations may enter vents connected to black markets alone
- Immunes may freely enter CTZ Vending Machine market.
- Combative units in groups of 2 may enter the shaft to deal with any confirmed threat within it, loitering inside is prohibited.

The "tram blackmarket" is not considered "blackmarket ventilation". If there are confirmed hostiles within it, combative units may clear it out but must exit immediately after.

##### **Ventilation not connected to Black markets**

Many ventilation systems found around the site are not connected to any high-traffic areas such as black markets however they do still have their own set of rules.

- These systems may be accessed by combative units freely.
- Non-combative personnel for the use of shorter routes/travel between locked down areas.

##### **CISCZ Black market vents**

The ventilations system within CISCZ is entirely connected to the black-market since there are 3 locations the black-market rotates through. All vents in and surrounding the CISCZ are to be considered “connected to a black-market” as there is no way to pre-determine where the black-market spawns.

---

#### TSCZ Black-market Lockdown

In some special circumstances, the black market lock down for the TSCZ may be enabled by non-combative personnel. This LD may stay on for a maximum of 15 minutes, and has a cool down of 15 minutes to be turned on again.
Classrooms (Seminar wing) lockdown has the same restrictions as the BM Lockdown and can be activated as well if conditions below are met. (It may still be closed when S2 Partial is engaged.)

The LD may only be enabled if the following conditions apply:

- Non-combative personnel (L3+) hosting a mass event (Mass interview, mass checkup, etc.)
- RsD Organizing/Starting any type of test

Due to the nature of the events the BM LD should be used for, its use is restricted to L-3+ personnel hosting those events.

- L-4+ personnel may grant permission to lower-ranking personnel within their department to use the BM LD in use-cases outside of mass-events

All activations of the BM LD should be announced via the radio system using an “@combatives ” ping. This is to ensure all security personnel are aware of its activation.

Note: The BM LD should never be used by combative personnel. (Except during raids)

---

#### Sector 1 Med-bay Lockdown

In the event of an ongoing Site Emergency, Medical personnel may lockdown the Sector 1 Med-bay for the purpose of keeping all occupants inside safe. During this time it may act as a safe area just as a panic shelter would.

The following criteria for a lockdown are as listed:

- There is a confirmed threat inside of Sector 1.
- The current site code is set to GAMMA or above.

When medical personnel are to lockdown the Med-bay, it needs to be announced over Radio for other staff members or Security personnel.

The Sector 1 Med-bay may also be locked down by the order of MD HR+ without needing any of the 2 previous criteria's being met.

---

#### Sector Lockdown

In the event of a threat/incident affecting S1/S2, a lock down of the area may be used in various ways and may only be used for the following reasons:

- A breached specimen has been confirmed to be located within the sector/is confirmed to be heading to the sector.
- A large amount of inmates have breached the sector, and combatants have lost control of it for over 10 minutes.
  A full lock down of the sector in the event of a mass breach or a Code Gamma+ Test Subject riot, and if there is an L5+, GoI SHR+, or Combative/combative divisional HR+ to monitor/control the lock down usage.
  - The definition of a full sector lock down is closing all of the window grates and all blast doors within S2. In S1, a full sector LD would be closing all blast doors within Sector 1.

Standalone usage of blast doors or window graters are not allowed unless there is a **Code Red+** active. Combatants may modify the lock downs of the sectors if they deem it necessary.

After the following threats have been dealt with, or procedures are done, the lock down must be turned off immediately/procedure must be concluded. **The TSCZ lock down may not be enabled during system riots as it has been ordered by the Site Administrator.**

---

### CTZ lockdown

In the event of a CTZ containment breach or other hostiles within the sector, the CTZ lockdown may be enabled, locking the 2 main entrances, either trapping hostiles inside or keeping them out. The CTZ LD may only be used for the following reasons:

- 3+ hostiles enroute to the sector (tram BM onwards)
- 3+ hostiles are inside of the sector
- Any amount of hostiles are enroute using vehicles
- Any amount of hostiles are inside of the sector with a vehicle
- A breach is taking place in the sector
- May also be turned on if requested by an RSD due to either riskiness of a test, or to keep a large scale test in CTZ safe
  - a "risky" test would be defined as a test that may require large amounts (3-5) of infected to be let loose in CTZ for the test. Or if U4 specimens are being used in CTZ (outside of U4)
  - Large scale tests would be a mass test using any large area of CTZ as their "test chamber"
- JU operatives whenever they deem necessary, given they can provide valid reasoning

After the incident that caused the lockdown is resolved, the lockdown may be left on for an additional 5 minutes to ensure no more problems arise, after which it is to be turned off.

---

### CTZ contingency procedures

#### Bridge operation

During any and all codes, the CTZ Bridge must remain up, regardless of code. Any and all personnel should announce when they're using the CTZ Bridge, to avoid confusion if a hostile threat is using the bridge.
If a security checkpoint is being run by the bridge (Inner CTZ, main bridge, CTZ entrance road) it may remain down upon request of the unit guarding the closest checkpoint to it.

#### Chamber Lockdowns

Individual chambers may only be locked down in these instances:

- If an active breach had been just cleared of that specific specimen.
  - Example: There was a 990 breach that was just cleared, the 990 chamber can be put in lockdown.
- A large group (4-6) of TS have been spotted heading to CTZ in attempt to breach.

May stay on until the immune combatives have deemed it safe for it to be unlocked down.

---

### Blackout

Deactivation of the site’s lighting may be utilized as a last resort effort from site security to regain stability of the site. The authority to enable the blackout protocol is only given to high ranking security force members (L4+ or GoI officer rank equivalent), specialized unit MR+ (Special Operations and the Recontainment Unit) and the Juggernaut Unit.

Before the blackout protocol is enabled, it must be announced on the PA system, stating who authorized it. The protocol may be announced in the name of the authorizing officer but the said officer must be on-duty (in-game.) The following are valid reasons for the blackout protocol to be enabled:

- An armed riot has spread outside of the TSCZ, or a breach has made it out of the CTZ which has caused the loss of a sector and has not been contained within 25 minutes.

The lights may only be turned off for up to 15 minutes before they must be turned back on again. If the situation which has caused the blackout has not yet been handled, the time is extended until the threat is eliminated. **Blackouts may not be used in System Riots.**

**Note:** The lights should never be turned off during raids due to the vast majority of hostiles being equipped with night-vision which would heavily reduce the effectiveness of allied security forces.
cards.name: Rule B5 | PA, Vent & Contingency System Guidelines

cards.desc:
During all raids conducted by hostile forces, a set of **universal rules** will be present to keep all things fair and balanced between both parties. During any raid of any kind the following regulations apply:

- The Sector 1 LD should **not** be utilized in any way. (Blast doors, window shutters) but Sector 2 **partial** LD may be used during **loud raids**. (S2 L2 door + cargo elevator blast doors + shutters)
  - This does not apply to the TSCZ LD or CTZ LD
  - In the instance EPSILON is enabled, the S2 LD must be disabled.
  - The Black-market Lockdown may be utilized during any raid
- Any unfair advantages of any kind (Bugs, glitches, any other unintentional feature) may not be utilized during raids and can result in further punishment from the in-game moderation team.
- A 1:1 Ratio must be kept between Juggernaut Units and the hostile forces equivalent of it **with the sole exception of Centurion Raids, which has different ratio regulations.**
- Both parties must be respectful to each other and section A is always in effect for both parties, hostile or not.
- Stuns may not be utilized in any way. (Bat stun, stunstick stun, riot shield stun, etc…)
- Chem-bombing is not allowed to be utilized in any way.
- **During a breach**, BOTH PARTIES in a raid must ceasefire on each other, and deal with the breach. UN may assist in dealing with the breach if approved by TSC raid leaders. Flags must not be capped for the duration of the ceasefire.
- **Any** usage of traps on teleports and spawns is strictly prohibited during raids.

During Loud Raids, which are always announced beforehand, additional regulations apply:

- Special forces' squads may not be deployed on either side (Special Operations, Special Service Group). **This does not count for SO Tactical Response and base SSG units.**

Raids are classified into 2 different categories. “Loud Raids” and “Alternative Raids”. Loud raids are as they are, alternative raids are Flash, Stealth, and Solo raids.

- **2** Loud raids max per week (_Sunday 00:00 UTC -> Sunday 00:00 UTC_)
  - **2** day cooldown
- **7** alternative raids max per week(s)
  - **4** hour universal cooldown
- Mercenary (“Merc”) deployments have a cooldown of **1 hour**
- There is a 2 hour cooldown between UN events being hosted.

### **Regulations regarding more specifics are listed here;**

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bkC26zcUHJjEhN6KvObE6Kq2lM8kFLRHxXa6ek3wu4g/preview?tab=t.0

It is recommended that an ER member is present during any raid, especially loud raids, to keep track of the combatant ratio.

**Security personnel may not go past the Canadian border leading to the UNSDF spawn to deal with hostiles at any time during an active raid. Doing so will result in punishment for Illegal immigration.**
An example of where the border is can be found below.
cards.name: Rule B6 | Raid Regulations

cards.desc:
Vehicles may only be used for the transport of all personnel.

Personnel with a clearance level of 2 or higher within the department they are currently deployed as may operate vehicles.

- SD Carts and Security Jeeps may only be driven by combative personnel
- The Buggy, Golf Cart and Civilian Jeep may be driven by both combative and non-combative personnel
- The RECON Cart and BWD cart may only be driven by their respective members
- The Heavy Transport Truck may only be driven by Technical Task Squad operatives
- The Bus and all of its counterparts may only be used for non-combative events or rally events for transport.

Operating any vehicle without the correct clearance or exception to do so will result in punishment.

While operating any vehicle you must not deliberately crash it or recklessly operate it at speeds where it is likely to crash or intentionally run personnel over. You are also required to drive vehicles on roads or dedicated paths for vehicles, and you may not drive them on pedestrian walkways or anywhere where a vehicle does not belong. Small vehicles, like carts and buggies may be driven on walkways and other places as long as the driver of the vehicle is not being disruptive with the vehicle or a risk of harm to others by doing so.

Combatants may bypass vehicle driving regulations at their own discretion. If a combatant is to commit a violation of the vehicle driving regulations they must have their sirens activated. If the combatant must act immediately and cannot activate their sirens they will not be punished as long as there is valid reason for it. Abuse of this will lead to punishment.

To avoid incidents an individual is not to:

- Stand on top of vehicles while they are being operated
- Block the path or lunge in the way of the vehicle while it’s being operated
- Shoot the vehicle unless a hostile has control of it
- Throw anything at the vehicle that make cause damage to it or cause it to crash

The person who possesses the Car Keys of a vehicle is the owner of the vehicle. The owner’s name would be clearly visible on the license plates located on the front and rear of the vehicle.

If someone is found driving a car without permission from the owner, it would be considered a Grand Theft Auto crime unless exigent circumstances exist such as vehicle recovery after being stolen by hostiles or moving it out of the way of the train system or roadway. Combatants may borrow vehicles of others without their permission if it’s needed for emergency purposes only.
cards.name: Rule B7 | Vehicle Operation Regulations

cards.desc:
Following it’s activation the Black Market Lockdown (BM LD) stays on for a maximum of 15 minutes to help hosted events proceed without much interference. After the BM LD has been deactivated, either manually or automatically, a period of 15 minutes must pass before it can be activated again.

The BM LD should only be used sparingly and under specific circumstances to avoid abuse:

- RSD Mass Testing
- RSD U4 Testing
- Other forms of mass-events if TS are being disruptive
  - This includes: Mass checkups, mass tours, mass interviews, rallies, etc.

All activations of the BM LD should be announced via the radio system using an “@combatives ” ping. This is to ensure all security personnel are aware of its activation.

Due to the nature of the events the BM LD should be used for, its use is restricted to L-3+ personnel hosting those events.

- L-4+ personnel may grant permission to lower-ranking personnel within their department to use the BM LD in use-cases outside of mass-events

The BM LD should only be used outside of these circumstances if TS are being so disruptive as to make even normal non-combative events impossible to conduct.

Note: The BM LD should never be used by combative personnel
cards.name: Rule B8 | Blackmarket Lockdown

cards.desc:
To ensure that minimal danger is posed, the following should be upheld in the interest of the health and safety of all site personnel:

- Personnel should not deliberately put other personnel in harm's way. This includes overall refusal to perform departmental duties that result in putting other personnel at risk.
- Non-combatants should avoid active conflict zones where security forces are engaging any hostile forces. Intentionally entering and loitering in an active conflict zone is strictly prohibited. If the active conflict zone is a breach and a non-combatant refuses to leave the area, security members may shoot and terminate the non-combatant.
- Personnel must show ID papers at the request of any combatant or semi-combatant given their team possesses them. Failure to abide by this request in a reasonable timeframe grants the requester permission to, if need be, down and wand the questioned personnel.
  - Combatives/Semi-combatives are to make it clear they are asking for ID papers before firing upon the suspected disguised personnel.
  - The above can be bypassed if you have reasonable suspicion that the person is a disguised personnel.
  - Personnel that cannot speak to each other as per the ROBLOX chat restrictions may wand suspected disguised personnel.
- During TSCZ Lockdowns, non-combatives are to remain outside of the TSCZ _unless_ it is confirmed to be safe enough to enter for duty purposes.
  - Additionally, non-combatives who do go into the TSCZ during a lockdown must listen to combatives when asked to leave for a valid reason.
    - Valid reason including but not limited to; danger still being present and other combatives able to do the job the non-combative is there for.

If a personnel consents to said actions, you maybe break certain sections of C4/B3 that relate to harming said individual. These sections include;

- B3, "Innocent individuals may not be injured with any weapon". You are allowed to punch/hurts others if they **consent** to it and you aren't causing a disturbance.
  - Disturbance may be defined as something such as, fighting in the inner TSCZ where combatives are attempting to do their job (doesn’t mean you can do it when TSCZ is understaffed)
  - This may only be allowed when there are minimal people around, and you are not violating things such as behavioral guidelines from your department.
- C4, "While operating any vehicle you must not deliberately crash it or recklessly operate it at speeds where it is likely to crash or intentionally run personnel over." Personnel may be harmed with a vehicle if you have their consent to do so. This also should not be done while others are around or if there is a risk of harming other individuals.

If you are using these exceptions to mess around while on a combative team during an active emergency, it will be a violation of the rule above, “Personnel should not deliberately put other personnel in harm's way. This includes overall refusal to perform departmental duties.”

Note: It is highly recommended to maintain a safe distance from any object or person that poses a threat to themselves or the people around them. Failure to adhere to this can result in serious injury or death at the fault of the individual.

---

By signing the **liability waiver** that is commonly found around the facility, you consent to the fact that any other personnel _who have the waiver signed_ may engage in combat with you (without the use of firearms) at any given moment, and they are not to suffer any punishment for the damage inflicted.

**Note:** You are still not to cause any disturbance; for that, refer to the guidelines above.

---

Usage of Instance-294  during non-testing is restricted to personnel with a security clearance level of 3 or higher. Any personnel supervised by someone with clearance level 4 or higher may also use the instance.

For the safety of site personnel, only ordinary food items may be ordered from Instance-294 outside of testing purposes following the restrictions above. These items must not cause death or grant permanent statistical changes to your person (Such as Cup of More health, etc…).

- “Cup of player” during a test may not be used to harm any personnel or terminate uninfected test subjects.

If there are CIS present within Unit 3 then at least 1 combatant should escort non-combatant personnel using the machine to ensure their safety.

- Non-combatives that are immune do not require escort if CIS are present.

Additionally, members of the Psychology Branch may use Instance-294 to dispense Class-D items for therapeutic purposes.

---

The blender may be used by any personnel who has access to a blender location within the facility. Usage of the blender in a location that has limited access, such as the inner TSCZ, is not a valid reason to enter that location.

- Under no circumstances should you blend department or GOI-issued tools or equipment.

---

All members of the Medical Department ranked Nurse+ are permitted to enter combat zones at their own risk to assist Security personnel through healing and recovery with the understanding that they should remain behind Security as to not get in the way.

- They may also remain outside of panic shelters at their own risk in order to actively support security personnel on all code levels outside of Epsilon or Delta.
- They may enter areas they normally are not allowed to enter due to their security clearance or non-combatant status as long as they are actively supporting Security personnel with the exception of the Warhead Silo and Unit 4 unless given permission by the respective authority in those sectors.
- They may also accompany patrols of Security personnel throughout the facility in order to be readily available to provide aid only when necessary.
- Nurse+ may freely assist combatives during raids. However, if they are not actively assisting security forces then they must be in a panic shelter.  Nursing students may not assist in raids, and Interns may not be deployed during a raid period.
cards.name: Rule C1 | Physical & Mental Harm

cards.desc:
### General Hazardous Containment Zone Procedures (CTZ)

When entering any containment zone of a biohazard the following requirements must be met by personnel upon entering them:

- Personnel has full or partial immunity
- Non-combatant escorted by at least 2 non-immune combatants or 1 immune combatant
- No active or unrestrained specimens are currently inside the containment chamber

If the risk involved is deemed too great by escorting security staff, non-combatants may be prohibited from entering the containment zone.

Only Level-3 Personnel may enter the Containment Zone (CTZ). RSD, U&M, Combatant Personnel, EC, ISB, and MD(VP & PB) may bypass the clearance level restriction to enter the CTZ/CISCZ if it's required to fulfill their duties.

### **CISCZ / Unit 3 Procedures**

The CISCZ and Unit 3 extension house mostly docile infected specimens that are researched by the facility and must be handled with extra caution. The following rules apply to the CISCZ and by extension the Unit 3 area when CIS are present:

- Non-combatants may only reside on the top floor of the CISCZ if there is at least one combatant present in the CISCZ and must leave if there are none present. They may enter to determine if there is a combatant present, but are not allowed to loiter around any longer and are to stay behind the yellow line.
  - To determine where you cannot go, there will be signs above doors that will say something along the lines of “biohazard zone ahead” with red lettering.
- Combatants with full/partial immunity may enter the bottom floor of the CISCZ freely.
- Non-combatants may only enter the bottom floor of the CISCZ if they have permission from the combatant personnel present and with 1 partially/fully immune combatant escorting them.
- CIP and immune non-combatants may enter the bottom floor of the CISCZ freely.
- Non-immune combatants are only allowed on the bottom floor of the CISCZ if they are given explicit permission by Recontainment Unit members with valid reasoning, or any other immune combatants if they are absent. If there are no immunes present, they may enter the bottom floor if it is necessary to do their duties with good reason (Hostiles roaming the bottom floor, sweeping for escaped inmates...).

### Builds in the CISCZ

In order to have decorative & harmless builds not be needlessly destroyed, buildings in the CISCZ are protected by the CoE whether they be built by CIS or TS and may **only** be destroyed if they’re disrupting combative duties; Being used as cover, obstructing important sightlines etc.

‌

Combatant personnel reserve the right to tell any non-combatant personnel to leave the CISCZ or Unit 3 if they are acting in a disruptive manner or if there is any other danger imminent. RECON holds the highest authority over the CISCZ and Unit 3 when CIS are present during all codes below blue. This may change depending on the situation and they are to refer to the Security Department Chain of Authority in this scenario.

### Test Subject Containment Zone Procedures (TSCZ)

The TSCZ is a place where you will find most of the usually volatile Test Subjects. It starts from the break room exit to the inner TSCZ and goes all through up until the exit to the pool locker room which is located past the bathrooms. Due to the containment zone's erratic inmates, personnel should not enter the TSCZ unless they match one of the following:

- A combatant
- Intelligence personnel (EC, ISB)
- Personnel who have a clearance of Level-2 or higher
- Personnel who have a clearance of Level-1 which are being supervised by another individual which possesses a clearance of Level-3 or higher for the purpose of doing departmental duties.

Non-combatant personnel MUST stay behind the red combatant line unless they have a valid reason to pass.

- Valid reasons to cross include; U&M duties, MD personnel actively assisting combative personnel, etc.
- Escorted by 2 combatant personnel OR have designated VIP protection.
  - Designated VIP protection is considered any **regulated protection** such as JU, SO or ISB protection.
  - Semi-combatives **do** count as “combatant personnel”.

Personnel who do cross the red line (with one of the clauses stated above) are doing so at their own risk.

CIP should not pass the red line during an active breach due to a high chance of being misidentified or injured from anti-bio hazard tools. Under no circumstances can a CIP pass the red line during an active breach of Specimen-239.
cards.name: Rule C2 | Containment Zone Procedures

cards.desc:
Certain accessory items are prohibited from wear by inmates and corporation personnel to prevent inhibition of combatant judgement and maintain decency in the facility. These include:

- Full-body packages that disrupt shirts
- Large accessories that cover the body
- Shirts or pants that look like another department's clothing
- Outfits that imitate any hostile group
- Suggestive items such as Collars, or Bypassed UGC

Personnel and Inmates wearing such cosmetics should be detained and asked to unequip the offending items. If the personnel refuses to remove the offending item they may be infracted. If an inmate refuses they are considered KOS until they remove the offending item(s).

Personnel are to not wear disguises even if the disguise is of their team.

---

## Leaked Assets

Combatants may freely terminate anyone wearing leaked Thunder Scientific Corporation assets and _actively attempting to appear as infected_ through means of add-on accessories, even if the avatar (whether intentional or not) is not entirely identical to that of an infected, regardless of whether they are test subjects or personnel.

**This applies strictly to leaked infected assets.** Any other accessory does not justify termination. In cases where someone is wrongfully terminated, the terminating individual will face consequences.

**Note:** Wearing any of the leaked assets listed below on the Test Subject team makes you liable for in-game moderation action as well.
[https://trello.com/c/iZ3FcFjE/48-player-accessories](https://trello.com/c/iZ3FcFjE/48-player-accessories "smartCard-inline")

cards.desc:
Vehicles may only be used for the transport of all personnel.

Personnel with a clearance level of 2 or higher within the department they are currently deployed may operate vehicles.

Some vehicles are reserved for their division/department or Group of Interest. A list of those exemptions will be listed down below. Any vehicle that is not listed here can be driven freely by authorized individuals.

- SD Carts and Security Jeeps may only be driven by combatant personnel
- The RECON Cart may only be driven by their respective members
- The Maxi Delivery Cart may only be driven by Maxiburger members
- The SO Jeep may only be driven by Special Operations members
- The Heavy Transport Truck and TTS Cart may only be driven by Technical Task Squad operatives
- The Bus and all of its counterparts may only be used for non-combatant events or rally events for transport.
- The ISB Jeep as well as the ISB Bus may only be spawned in for member of the Internal Security Bureau. ISB Agents may authorize others to use them.
- HWY-P Trucks can be freely driven. However, usage of their sirens whilst not being teamed HWY-P is prohibited.
- The ambulance may only be used by medical personnel.
- The RECON copter may only be used by RECON & RAH.

Operating any vehicle without the correct clearance or exception to do so will result in punishment. Combatives are permitted to bypass the above rule if they need to commandeer a vehicle for emergency reasons (crisis far away, hostiles attempting to steal car, chasing hostiles, etc.).

While operating any vehicle you must not deliberately crash it or recklessly operate it at speeds where it is likely to crash or intentionally run personnel over. You are also required to drive vehicles on roads or dedicated paths for vehicles and you may not drive them on pedestrian walkways or anywhere where a vehicle does not belong (vehicles may be driven into the TSCZ briefing rooms for event transportation purposes). Small vehicles like carts and buggies may be driven on walkways and other places as long as the driver of the vehicle is not being disruptive with the vehicle or a risk of harm to others by doing so.

Combatants may bypass vehicle driving regulations at their discretion. If a combatant is to violate the vehicle driving regulations they must have their sirens activated if the vehicle is equipped with them. If the combatant must act immediately and cannot activate their sirens they will not be punished as long as there is valid reason for it. Abuse of this will lead to punishment.

To avoid incidents an individual is not to:

- Stand on top of vehicles while they are being operated
- Block the path or lunge in the way of the vehicle while it’s being operated
- Shoot the vehicle unless a hostile has control of it or the owner is no longer in-game
  - The owner’s name of the vehicle is visible on the license plates located on the front and rear of the vehicle.
- Throw anything at the vehicle that will cause damage to it or cause it to crash

If someone is found driving a car without permission from the owner, it would be considered a Grand Theft Auto crime unless exigent circumstances exist such as vehicle recovery after being stolen by hostiles or moving it out of the way of the train system or roadway. Combatants may borrow vehicles of others without their permission if it’s needed for emergency purposes only.

---

## Train regulations

The train that spawns in the map may be used for transportation around the site. However, there is a small set of rules you must abide to when operating/going to be operating the train.

- U&M Conductors may drive the train freely (as long as they are following their rules)
- L2+ may drive the train within reason.
  - Whilst there is an ongoing emergency, any security personnel (Full-combatives) may operate the train if needed.
- The person who drives the train must be courteous to those who would like to use it to go places (You should know if you drive the train, people will want to use it to taxi around. Don't hog the train.)
- Whoever finds the train first may drive it unless;
  - Another person who would like to drive it is a conductor, in which you must hand it over to them
  - There is a large event happening such as a rally, patrol, etc. and they would like to use it
  - Combatives require it during an emergency on-site and must get somewhere quickly.
- You should not be using the train to get places you are not permitted.
- The train is to be driven carefully and at controllable speeds so that it does not crash.

---

## Gyrocopter regulations

The gyrocopter is a helicopter which can be obtained through the SD garage that may be used for flight around the site. Since flying is dangerous, there are regulations in place for flying the gyrocopter.

- The gyrocopter may be freely flown by combative personnel that hold an L3+ clearance.
  - Non-combative personnel that hold an L4+ clearance, an L4 equivalent in a **friendly** GoI or Intelligence personnel may fly the gyrocopter freely as well.
  - An exemption for this rule is made for Highway Patrol personnel who have completed their gyrocopter certification.
- You should not use the gyrocopter to get places you are not permitted.
- The gyrocopter may not be flown in high population areas. (E.g. TSCZ or CISCZ)
- The gyrocopter should be driven at a controllable speeds to limit crashing.
  - In the event that the gyrocopter crashes and the blades fall off, you are expected to discard of them within any bin as soon as you can.
  - If your team regulations allow for the rotor blade to be used for combat instead, then you are allowed to use it.
- The Research & Studies Department may freely use the gyrocopter for testing purposes.

For the safety of non-combatant personnel, during times they are taken hostage the following regulations should be followed to ensure no unnecessary damage is caused to hostages. The following document details these regulations and can be found here:

[https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Iy9Wccg8Pj5t3p5uo5acBRC_Sl1ZlhnqJKshUjipCdY/edit](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Iy9Wccg8Pj5t3p5uo5acBRC_Sl1ZlhnqJKshUjipCdY/edit "smartCard-inline")
