cards.name: Rule C5 | Hostage Regulations

cards.desc:
Inmates held in Corporation sites are to follow a strict behavioral code. Failure to do so may result in a termination of the Subject.

‌

- Security Department Personnel may follow their termination guidelines in their own handbook, even if they are not found here in the Code of Ethics. The handbook may be found here: [https://trello.com/b/t7X77BIf/tsc-security-department-handbook](https://trello.com/b/t7X77BIf/tsc-security-department-handbook "smartCard-inline")

Inmates must be terminated under the following conditions:

- An inmate is outside their containment zone without a valid escort or a proper tag for a site event.
  - Combatants reserve the right to not terminate and instead re-capture a subject if they are found outside of their containment zone and not showing any signs of hostility. During EOP Red+ combatants must terminate all roaming subjects.
- An inmate is over their containment zone’s kill line or climbing.
  - Inmates that are pushing, throwing, or carrying others over the termination line are liable for termination.,
  - Inmates who have been pushed over the line follow a 3 second grace period to move off the line before termination, and those who were thrown or carried are to be taken back over the line.
- The inmate has contraband.
- The inmate is wearing a large accessory that inhibits a combatant’s ability to see whether or not they are carrying contraband or are wearing accessories that look like contraband or is wearing an accessory covering their entire avatar or more.
  - Inmates that wear outfits that resemble any hostile teams may be downed as a precaution by combatants if there are any doubts in the true allegiance of the subject.
  - Inmates that wear accessories that are considered leaked infected assets and that are actively attempting to mimic an infected (refer to C3 for more information on such assets).
- An inmate is hostile towards personnel or other inmates.
  - Inmates may act hostile towards each other if in the boxing ring or have signed the liability waiver.
- Inmates are using the fire extinguisher in a hostile or disruptive manner (examples: Spraying it over the line, using it to obscure combatives vision, etc.)
- Inmates are destroying equipment belonging to personnel or corporation equipment.
- The inmate is actively assisting other hostile inmates. This includes but is not limited to healing, reviving, shielding, or giving items for purposes of extended hostility.
- The inmate is outside of the cell blocks during a TSCZ lockdown.
  - TSE Surgeons can be allowed outside the cellblocks as long as they remain inside the TSCZ med-bay and do not let other subjects inside.
  - Combatant L4+ may authorize security forces to cuff and relocate test subjects to a secure location to deal with breaches within the TSCZ cellblocks.
- The inmate is outside their containment zone during a raid. (Regardless of the presence of an escort.)
- An inmate is showing signs of progressing infection (of any hazard; radiation, specimen infection, etc.) within their containment zone without the ability to decontaminate them immediately.
- The inmate is on the kill-line and refuses to move off of it after a warning shot.
- An inmate is opening a ventilation shaft or manhole or is standing within proximity (5 studs) of a ventilation shaft or manhole. This increases to 15 studs when the ventilation shaft is open. (One stud is an R6 character’s arm-width).
  - Images showing the limit of the 5 studs and 15 studs radius can be found at the bottom of this section. When an inmate crosses into this threshold, with the intention to open/enter a vent or not, they are considered KoS.
  - Note: The “impossible vent” is not an escape route and therefore does not apply to this instance.
  - Combatants reserve the right to disperse test subjects away from the proximity of an escape route as long as there are 3 or more subjects near it. If the test subjects fail to move away from a 15-stud distance of the escape route they may be terminated.
  - Inmates actively running towards an open escape route may be downed by combatants.
- An inmate is currently under any long-lasting visual or statistic-altering effects outside of testing. (examples: extra health, height changes, mutations, etc.)
  - Height changes from eating sandwiches do NOT count towards this.
- The inmate is covering another inmate that’s opening an escape route.
- The inmate is actively utilizing moving objects to obstruct escape routes.
- The inmate is actively throwing mass amounts of any item around.
- The inmate is undergoing an MD Pale Virus examination, and the MD personnel in charge has concluded the event and have requested their termination.
- An inmate is located outside the cell blocks during a system riot.
- Inmates who are due for SC may be **stunned** in order to grab them more easily.
- An inmate is lighting grease on fire to purposefully block off areas or obstruct combatives.
- Inmates that are within 10 studs of downed personnel may be stunned, they may instead be downed if they’re within 10 studs and have a melee weapon out.

Note: You must confirm that an inmate has performed any of the actions listed above before termination. Termination based on assumption is prohibited. This does not apply to the 294 effects sub-point.

---

### Building

Inmates who possess the ability to use the building system have additional conditions for termination:

- Fortification of Places of Interest or using props to aid inmates in terminable offense(s) or escape from termination.
  - Blocking off entrances and passages (Doors, Hallways, Ladders, Vents, etc.)
  - Creating builds meant to give advantage to inmates in fighting or fleeing combatants
- Moving or tinkering with props that combatant engineers have placed to make a cover.
- Moving or tinkering with props while combatants are trying to destroy/move them.
- Creating structures that may allow for inmates to gain access to restricted areas.
- Creating structures that intentionally obstruct combative sightlines to the vents, kill line, or from any other area needed to be actively monitored.

TSCZ is an area where Unauthorized Engineers (UE) may freely create structures given they are not violating what is said above, or their own building regulations. Any builds that do not grant access to unauthorized areas or do not violate the termination conditions listed should not be destroyed normally. (See **Note** below)

**Note:** SET staff may destroy buildings built or compromised by test subjects during Code Red+ or during their "Base Destroyer" event.

---

### Contraband

Access cards, black market dead drop packages, items that can assist in opening ventilation or doors, and weaponry count as contraband. Items used for medical and recreational purposes are not with the exception of research vials and MD’s tools.

- Items that allow test subjects to enter an authorized location such as the Kitchen-Clearance or TSE Surgeon tool are also not considered contraband.
- Decoy Rifles, found in Aleks's Sandwich Stand in the SD armory, may only be bought by members of combatant departments. Additionally, they may only be used in logical situations, thus throwing them around with no intent of combat use is prohibited. Giving them freely to TS or members of non-combative departments is also prohibited. They are to be treated as contraband for TS.
- The “War Banner” tool is not to be considered contraband as it is purely cosmetic and has lower damage then fists.

---

### Bounties

Inmates attempting to obtain contraband from a deceased inmate by moving to stand on or right beside them may be terminated at the discretion of the security personnel.

Inmates with a valid KoS (Kill on Sight) order against them may be terminated anywhere at any time until the order expires. There must be special consideration to not kill them until they leave spawn to prevent spawn killing. Inmates also automatically gain a valid KoS order if they have over a $1,200 bounty and may be killed anywhere for the duration of the bounty.

- ISB agents engaging in bounty hunting may terminate any subject with any amount of accumulated bounty posted.

---

### Stacking

Test Subjects/Contained Infected Subjects are not to be killed or harmed for stacking unless they are caught doing it to escape or get somewhere they are not supposed to be (catwalks, balcony, any TSCZ overlooks, CISCZ balcony, any of the player-count monitors).

- An exception is made for the damaged watchtower with a garbage incinerator near the gym in the TSCZ.

_TS/CIS may be shot/hit as a warning if they are attempting to stack to any of the mentioned places._

Due to the layout of the CISCZ making it easy to escape by stacking, CIS will have less leniency and should be warned to stop stacking if they are doing it near the balcony and killed if they continue to do so.

---

### Surgeon Med-bay Exemption

TSE Surgeons are the only test subjects permitted to enter the med-bay inside TSCZ outside of medical checkups, as well as being able to obtain and carry MD tools without being considered contraband.

- Medical personnel may force out TSE Surgeons with the help of Security Forces if it is needed for an event or they are being disruptive. Surgeons may still enter to get MD tools as long as they immediately leave during this time.
- TS who are disruptively blocking the medical post door or windows may be downed and removed from the area at the discretion of the present Security Forces guarding the post or requested by the MD staffing the med-bay. Repeated attempts are cause for termination.
- TS who are attempting to get inside the med-bay or airlock without authorization may be terminated.

Medical Department members may tag up to 2 TSE Surgeons to sit behind the non-combative line and heal Personnel. They should not be terminated if they are tagged.

Test subjects may freely enter the Banquet hall and Pool room respectively.
cards.name: Rule D1 | Test Subject Procedures

cards.desc:
In order to deploy as Test Subject whilst being in a department/division you must complete the departments quota and complete the TS deployment requirement in the department/division that grants you your highest clearance. L4+ Personnel of a department/division who do not require permission to deploy on Test Subject team unless otherwise specified, may authorize people who are in a department/division to deploy as a Test Subject, even if they have not completed their quota.

Level 5+ personnel from that same department/division may order you to undeploy with valid reasoning unless a listed exception was met. A baseline for valid reasoning is the following:

- Deployment on Test Subject while they are on LoA in their departments
- Disciplinary action was taken upon personnel that involves TS deployment
- Department Co-Head+ from your highest department may force you off with their respective authority provided their reasoning does not contain any malicious intent

There is no restriction on how many times you may deploy in a week or for how long each time, however departments may set further restrictions on time and length.

Note: A baseline for these restrictions must be that departments/division must grant free TS deployment for at least **one day** upon completion of the departments/divisions quota.

Once ordered to undeploy with valid reasoning, there will be a period of 3 hours where personnel may not deploy on the Test Subject team. Once that cooldown has ended, they may not be ordered off the Test Subject team for the remainder of the day granted that they have met the requirements to deploy and are not on LoA or undergoing punishment that involves TS deployment.

- An exception is made for the Security Department's "One Life Rule" where personnel whose highest clearance comes from SD may not deploy on TS when the site EOP is Red+, or there is any other on-going emergency. Personnel who were on prior to the emergency may stay on TS for the remainder of their life. This rule also applies to members of the SD/U&M’s Security Engineering Team, if U&M or SD is their highest clearance department. The only exception to this rule is if the person is a High Class Test Subject/Steeleburger Guard+ or attending an official TSE event.

If authorized by your department, you may deploy at any time for any length of time. If the department your highest clearance is in allows this then L5+ personnel in other departments you are a member of may have you undeploy unless you have completed that department’s quota. This means permission from the next highest supersedes any orders to undeploy in departments granting lower clearance.

Note: If your highest clearance is granted through multiple departments at once, the departments whose rank is higher in accordance to the departments Chain of Authority takes priority. If the Chain of Authority is the same, the department whose member count is the highest restrictions apply.

High Class Test Subjects, Steeleburger Guard+, and Contained Infected Subject HRs may freely deploy on the Test Subject team without permission if they are in a department, however they may be forced off by their Department head or co-head to deploy on their department in accordance with the guidelines above.

- The exception for this is when they are hosting or co-hosting an official event for Test Subjects/Contained Infected Subjects.
- Trial High Class Test Subjects/Trialing Contained Infected Subject HRs are only exempt from deployment regulations when they are hosting or co-hosting an official event for Test Subjects.
- High Class Test Subjects/Steeleburger Guard+/Contained Infected Subjects HRs may be forced off by L5+ personnel in their highest clearance department if they have not completed their quota. It is important to note that they must be forced off personally and only used when necessary.

Note: In order to use the exception, proof must be shown that the HCTS/CIS HR in question are listed as either the host or co-host in the event announcement.

Department Co-Head+ are exempt from these regulations.

### TS Deployment Regulations for Lore Acting Department Members:

You may freely deploy on the Test Subject team, overriding TS deployment regulations from your other departments, if you are a member of the Lore Acting Department and you have a Test Subject acting character.

**Note:** You **MUST** be _in-character_ during the duration of your TS deployment.
If you're deploying on the Test Subject team _out of character_, you must follow TS deployment regulations from your highest ranking department.
cards.name: Rule D2 | TS Deployment

cards.desc:
Combatants may put rioting or excessively hostile TS in a cell for up to 20 minutes at a time depending on the situation. Without solitary confinement, securing the TSCZ would be extremely difficult as TS could cause problems immediately after they respawn. Due to limiting their capacity to perform actions certain rules apply:

- A “rioting” Test Subject is considered to be any TS who has received any amount of strikes.
  - Test subjects which riot during a System Riot event do not earn strikes for being terminated.
- A subject that has gained 3 strikes by violating D1 a total of 3 times (not necessarily being terminated) is subject to being put in solitary.
  - Strikes can be shown with the strike gun or combative may keep track of them on a notepad for each subject they see violating D1.
  - If you have access to the Strike Tracker, you are **strongly encouraged** **to use it** when are striking a Test Subject for violating D1. If you do not have access due to department restrictions, you should use `!notepad`
- If a Test Subject is found to be rioting a sufficient number of times, they will be put in Solitary Confinement for no less than 10 minutes and no more than 20 minutes at a time.
  - Non-Combatives may not mess with the Solitary Confinement timer at all.
- Strikes for Solitary Confinement have a 10-minute lifetime before being deemed invalid as long as the subject has not been rioting during those 10 minutes. Rioting is defined as being liable for termination as by D1.
- The combative who is to put a Test Subject into solitary is to be held responsible for releasing that same Test Subject on time. Failure to do so may result in consequences.
  - A 5-minute leeway should be given to allow the original combatant time to remove the Test Subject from Solitary.

Security Forces will normally follow the initial 3-strike rule unless otherwise stated by site protocols, which will evolve as additional time in Solitary Confinement progresses:

- There may be times that security forces may authorize placing a subject into solitary confinement for fewer instances of rioting.
- If a Test Subject continues to riot immediately after being released, they shall be returned to Solitary Confinement under a one-strike rule. “Immediately” is considered up to 10 minutes after being released from Solitary Confinement.

Contained Infected Subjects follow the same regulations as test subjects when it comes to solitary confinement.

---

**Heavy Solitary Confinement**

The Heavy Solitary Confinement Zone is a more secure location that requires 2 personnel to operate effectively and is to be used for cases when normal solitary confinement is not enough or if the subjects are particularly problematic. Guidelines for the use of Heavy Solitary are listed below:

- TS with an active KoS order has accumulated 2 strikes for SC
  - The KoS order itself does not count as a strike for this purpose
- TS has escaped from Solitary twice
  - There may be times when security forces may authorize Heavy Solitary for fewer escape attempts
- TS that has been placed into SC multiple times in the past 45 minutes
- A valid site protocol authorizes heavy solitary for fewer strikes than usual
- All standard Solitary rooms are filled

---

Note: Test Subjects may be downed to put them into Solitary Confinement as a last resort if it proves difficult to catch the subject running away or avoiding capture for Solitary Confinement.
cards.name: Rule D3 | Solitary Confinement

cards.desc:
The TSCZ is a place where you will find most of the usually volatile Test Subjects, and because of their nature regulations below have been put in place to prevent some casualties.

The TSCZ starts from the break room exit to the inner TSCZ, and goes all through up until the entrance to the pool locker room which is located past the bathrooms. The TSCZ also extends to the gate to the Banquet Hall and the doorway to the kitchen. These locations have additional requirements for test subjects to enter which will be listed later in this section.

Personnel should not enter the TSCZ unless they match at least one of the following:

- A combatant.
- A member of EC, ISB, or ER.
- Personnel of security clearance of 3 or higher.
- Personnel of security clearance of 2 may only enter for up to 10 minutes in order to do their departmental duties or perform simple tasks such as asking questions or letting others know of something. This 10 minute timer may be enforced by security personnel guarding TSCZ, but is recommended to be left to EC to handle it. Loitering with no business being inside is not permitted.

In the interest of safety and minimal distractions for security personnel, non-combatants should stay behind the red combative line unless there is a reasonable excuse to pass. Personnel who decide to cross it are to do so at their own risk and are recommended to have a security escort to ensure their safety.

Security personnel withhold the right to request non-combatants to leave the inner TSCZ, or TSCZ altogether if they are causing a disruption or are being a hazard to others.

- Exceptions include EC, ISB, ER, AD, and mod personnel if necessary to perform their duties.

CIP should not pass the red line during an active breach due to a high chance of being misidentified or injured from anti-biohazard tools. An immune security escort is recommended to ensure their safety or clean up a potential biohazard.

- Special note: Under no circumstances can a CIP pass the red line during an active breach of Specimen-239.

---

Test subjects may freely enter the Banquet hall. The Medbay located next to the banquet hall may only accessed by subjects who are undergoing a valid medical examination.

The TSCZ Kitchen may be freely accessed by test subjects who carry a kitchen-clearance card. Any subject who does not have a kitchen-clearance card is prohibited from entering the kitchen. Any personnel authorized to freely enter the TSCZ may freely access the kitchen, but is recommended to have a security escort due to the ease of access by test subjects.

The pool locker room and poolroom are able to be entered freely by test subjects but it is recommended that combatants actively protect it when there are a large group of subjects using the pool. Any of the hallways past the poolroom are restricted to test subjects.

The medical station inside the TSCZ Commons is restricted from subject access at all times and medical personnel should have at least 1 combatant present to ensure their safety inside the station.
cards.name: Rule D2 | Entering TS CZ

cards.desc:
### Contained Infected Subject and Infected Subject Information

Contained Infected Subjects are people hired to act as infected on-site. These users are the ones who are seen as infected’s in the Contained Infected Subject Containment Zone, and have been trained to act out being a character of their choosing. They can either be OOC (Out of Character) or IC (In-character) both of which have different regulations. OOC CIS would have their username showing as well as their CIS rank in their rank-tag. IC CIS will have “CIS-XXXX” and not have a rank-tag visible.
The other type of users you may see are people with the tags that only have “Infected” in them. These are Test Subjects that have not been hired to act, and are from tests that either an RSD or MD hosted; alongside this VP may take CIS to various locations within the site if escort ratios are followed. If within the CISCZ, escort rules can be relaxed, given a free-roam is authorized. VP may not take CIS to Sector 2 given alarm triggers and regulation contradictions. Rehabilitation events are ethically valid as long as a VP follows the requests of a CIS given they do not harm anyone. This is stated here to not cause confusion.

Summary:
IC = In-character (Acting as a character)
OOC = Out-of-Character (Not acting as any character)
IS = Infected Subject (an infected TS, not an actor)

While the rules below should be followed by all combatives, when dealing with infected individuals, you should attempt to find an immune combative to handle the situation if you are not immune.

---

### General Policy

When confronted with a CIS, you should not immediately start firing unless they are actively showing hostility towards you. (Shooting first, running at you with fists, etc.)

#### Encountering an IC CIS

IC CIS will normally be passive when encountered all have different reactions to personnel due to them being in-character. With them, you should also not fire immediately similar to the OOC encounter guidelines. However, instead of going straight to leading them back, you are allowed to make conversation with the subjects. Perhaps to find out why they may have escaped, if they would like to go back, stuff that will make the interaction more intriguing for both parties.
If you are not one for acting or interacting with the CIS, you may ask for an immune or another combative to handle the situation.
The CIS is to be brought back to CISCZ but more preferably with an immune/QIE (Qualified Infected Escort). If none are available at the time, you may cautiously bring the CIS back to containment.
When brought back to CISCZ, you may ask them to hand over any contraband they may have or check them with the wand before they are let back in.

- Items that are given through the “faction” system are not to be considered contraband if the CIS is wearing the appropriate uniform.
- Guns, such as the “Model-870” are still to be considered contraband.

In summary:

- Assess whether or not CIS is hostile
  - Hostile; attempt to have them stand down before firing upon them.
    - Hostility can be shown as harming you or others and running at you with any weapon (including fists).
    - Singular acts of hostility do not count as “hostile”.  Continuous acts do.
  - Passive; take time to interact with the subject. Ask for them to drop any contraband they may have.
    - If non-compliant, you are **NOT** to shoot at the CIS. Try to speak to them, or allow another combative to handle the situation.
- Call for an immune
  - No immunes; escort the CIS back to CISCZ without cuffs.
  - Immune response; have them take the CIS back and continue normal duties.

If the CIS you encounter has special abilities that would make recontaining more difficult, (Tiger shark speed, hypnosis, Squog endurance, etc.) you are able to take less precautions when handling the situation.
This means, you are able to be less lenient when assessing for hostility or non-compliance.

#### Encountering an OOC CIS / Chamber Infected

- OOC CIS follow all termination guidelines inside of D1 essentially making them TS, they will be KOS outside of CISCZ
- Chamber Infected will also follow all termination guidelines inside of D1, but will only be KOS outside of their respective chambers.

---

### **Infected Subject Termination Policies**

These subjects are not to be treated as lightly as actors. They are considered TS still and have termination policies similar to the ones stated in D1. These are the termination guidelines for Infected subjects.

- Showing hostility (harming any other person or subject, infecting personnel)
- Inside of the any ventilation, including BM
- Wielding any contraband
- Outside of inner CISCZ (On the road is considered OUTER CISCZ and may be terminated there)
- Using any vehicle
- Stacking more then 3 players (Punching bag counts as 1 player)
- Found in any area they are not authorized to be
  - Upper CISCZ or onto the ramp. They may be there if they have specific permission
- Caught breaking the cover in the ball pit
- Caught attempting to open BM vent
- Going onto rafters or any high places (following climbing rules)

Infected subjects that are within the CISCZ without the proper Immune ratios being met are permitted to be terminated; as they create a huge risk factor.

---

#### Climbing Rules

- Any CIS may use the vent into the spider wolf den, which is behind a bookcase in inner CISCZ. They are allowed to stay in the room it leads to, but cannot go into rafters itself.
- Any CIS may climb onto the rafters located in the pool section.

---

### Notes

CIS (both **OOC and IC**) that are currently under any long-lasting visual or statistic-altering effects (from any testing equipment such as the vending machine, static chamber, etc.) **outside of testing** are allowed to be terminated. (Examples of such effects being: extra health, height changes, etc.)
Before termination, you **must** have a reasonable suspicion that they are under the effects of the vending machine contents if you are not able to properly evaluate their stats. (Similar to the D1 regulation regarding TS and 294)
Ways to check include; medical personnel’s “Health Analyzer”, observing any speed increase/decrease, or observing whether they have grown/shrunk in height.

These are base guidelines for combatives who encounter any kind of IS/CIS. The immune combatives, (RECON) are to follow their guidelines that are stated in their handbook.
cards.name: Rule D4 | Contained Infected Subject Procedures

cards.desc:
The Contained Infected Subject Containment Zone (CISCZ) houses mostly docile specimen that are selected to be further studied by the corporation. Their docile nature does not eliminate their biohazard status and must still be handled with extra caution. The following rules apply to the CISCZ and by extension the Unit 3 area when CIS are present:

- Only personnel with a level 3 clearance or higher may enter the CISCZ.
- Non-combatants are permitted to remain inside the CISCZ on the top floor only when there’s at least one combatant present in the CISCZ. If the combatant leaves then the non-combatants must also leave until there is another present within the CISCZ. Personnel may enter to determine if there is a combatant present, but must leave once they find that there is none inside. This rule extends to Unit 3 only when CIS are present outside the CISCZ in Unit 3. Non-combatants are then to stay behind the yellow line when entering U3.
- Combatants with partial or full infection immunity are allowed to enter the bottom floor of the CISCZ for any reason.
- Non-combatants may only enter the bottom floor of the CISCZ with permission of the present combatants and an escort of at least 2 partially or fully immune to infection combatants.
- CIP (Contained Infected Personnel) and immune non-combatants may enter the bottom floor of CISCZ as they please as long as there is at least 1 combatant present within the CISCZ to watch over them.
- Non-immune combatants are not allowed on the bottom floor of the CISCZ unless they are given explicit permission by present Recontainment Unit personnel for a valid reason, or other immune combatants if RECON is absent. If no Immune combatants are present to grant permission then the bottom floor may be entered if it’s required to fulfill their duties with good reason. Duties are enumerated within the combatant's departmental handbook or GoI Contract and should not deviate from them unless there is an immediate exigent circumstance to do so. They may roam around the entirety of Unit 3 freely even with CIS presence.
- Combatants reserve the right to tell non-combative personnel to leave the CISCZ or Unit 3 if they are acting in a disruptive manner or are a hazard to themselves, the CIS, or others. If their safety is threatened by imminent or ongoing inmate aggression then they may also by told to leave.
- RECON has the highest authority within the CISCZ, and Unit 3 when CIS are present, during code green and blue. For all other codes or reasons RECON members are to refer to the Security Department Chain of Authority. Additionally, RECON are permitted to order any non-infection immune combatants out during aforementioned cases with good reason.
- RSD, U&M, EC, and ER may bypass the clearance level restriction to enter CISCZ if it's required to fulfill their duties.

The CISCZ officially begins at its door entrance within the Unit 3 Containment zone area. The top floor of the CISCZ begins from the door entrance and ends at the balcony overlooking the bottom floor, CISCZ Solitary, and the Observation room. Anything beyond that is classed as the “bottom floor”.

Unit 3 officially begins at the roadway gate and 2 side doors and ends at the CISCZ entrance and the Unit 4 checkpoint.
cards.name: Rule D3 | Entering CIS CZ

cards.desc:
Research and Studies Department personnel are permitted to violate all **except for** the Behavioral Guidelines and Abuse & Misconduct sections (A & F) of the Code of Ethics during active testing as long as all combative escorts consent to it and it doesn’t threaten site operations. _RsD personnel may violate section F if it's within reason, for example: giving TS weapons for a test procedure._

Additionally, RsD is freely permitted to test personnel with their consent. If a Researcher decides to use personnel, they are to fully abide by their wish to withdraw consent at any time.

If a section of the Code of Ethics is going to be violated, you must inform everyone present during the first briefing. This is to prevent anyone from being told too late or not told at all, which could lead to miscommunication and infractions, or slowing down the research efforts.

Ethics Committee Agents may intervene when there’s an actual threatening situation: the researcher is risking a breach, cramming infected into a tiny room, etc. Minor mistakes will attempt to be corrected first instead of shutting down the testing and RsD HRs will be contacted.

Note: This exemption only applies to the actual RsD performing the valid testing. RsD personnel will be held liable for Code of Ethics violations if their testing is unauthorized.

---

Ethics personnel withhold the right to shut down a test for the following reasons:

- The test or person responsible for the test is directly violating the Code of Ethics not outlined in the exceptions listed above
- The test is insufficiently secured for the risk involved, i.e. the test is not following RsD escort regulations:
- ⚬  _4 TS per each Primary / Secondary escort_
- ⚬  _5 TS per each High Priority escort_
- ⚬  _8 TS per each Juggernaut Unit (JU)_
- The test host is attempting to access a high-security area without the correct RsD ranking
- Test Subjects have not received a full briefing
- Site security level was set to code GAMMA or above

In an emergency, Ethics personnel can shut down a test for other reasons, given they can explain their actions afterward.

---

In the event of the EOP system being changed to code RED, the host must stop the event and evaluate if the threat is located in the sector their test is currently located in. If the threat is located within their sector, the following procedure must be carried out for the test by the present staff:

1. Inmates must either be terminated, returned to their containment zone, escorted to a secure location, or left at the site of the event at the discretion of security staff.
2. Present security staff should escort all non-combatant personnel present at the event to a safe area.
3. Once the event has been terminated and all staff are safe, security staff should proceed with their regular response to the type of incident,
4. If the test has already made its way to the Containment Zone and present combatants deem it safe enough to continue the test, the event may be continued.
cards.name: Rule E1 | Test Shutdowns

cards.desc:
Combatants should only ever decline escorting a test if they have a valid reason. Valid reasons for declining a test escort are as follows:

- The RsD requesting the test is an Trainee or if the MD requesting a checkup is below the rank of Nursing Student without a supervisor
- The TSCZ/CISCZ would not be properly secured without the combatants in question (At least 2 security must remain inside TSCZ to guard)
- The only available combatants do not have the necessary tools to secure the test
- There is currently an identified CIS or breached specimen in the TSCZ or around it
- The situation in TSCZ is nearing a riot OR there are multiple problematic TS causing problems within the TSCZ
- There is currently an event in which SD personnel are partaking UNLESS said event involves testing
- There is an identified breached and confirmed hostile specimen somewhere in the CTZ
- There is an ongoing sitewide emergency i.e.: Breach, Raid, Riot, CTZ Lockdown, etc...

If a combatant is seen denying test escorts for minuscule reasons, such as a personal grudge against the RsD in question, they will get infracted by EC. However, said combatant may be given more leniency on that, provided they have a good reason which is not specified on this list. If the reason provided by the combatant is seen as not fit, the combatant will be infracted.

---

During any on-site event, the combative ratio of Infected Subject (IS) or Test Subject (TS) should be the following:

Normal Security Forces : Test Subjects > 1:3

Recontainment Unit/Special Operations : Test Subjects > 1:4

Juggernaut Unit : Test Subjects > 1:8

Recontainment Unit/Technical Task Squad : Infected Subject  > 1:3

Juggernaut Unit : Infected Subjects > 1:6

Only paired RAH assets may escort hadron tests when requested by the host. RAH ratios are as follows:
Light Pairs: 1:6 Test Subjects, 1:4 Infected Subjects
Heavy Pairs: 1:8 Test Subjects, 1:6 Infected Subjects

Each combatant present in a test escort increases the maximum ratio by 1. Example being is if there’s 3 Normal Security Forces escorting a test, they would be able to escort 11 TS in total (3 + (3+1) + (3+1).

RSD Do not follow the rules above and instead have full control over their own escort ratios, further information about the ratios can be found in the [RSD Handbook](https://trello.com/c/Hk7ZOD2t/29-combatants-escorting "‌").
cards.name: Rule E2 | Combatant Escort Procedures

cards.desc:
Scientific equipment is the equipment found around the facility (such as the centrifuge, instance 294 (coffee machine), the acid pit, radiation chamber, static chamber, hadron collider, vehicle testing chamber, incinerator, and Unit 1 Labs.) and is meant for scientific testing and scientific testing alone except instance 294.

Misuse of scientific equipment would be:

- Using the equipment without the supervision of a scientist.
- Testing on the equipment without being a scientist.
- Using the equipment as a scientist during an unethical test.
- Abusing the equipment as a scientist in hopes of breaking it during a test.
- Abusing equipment as a non-scientist in hopes of sabotaging a test.
- Using the TSCZ testing queue buzzer outside of testing conditions.

These rules only apply to staff members and external combatants. (Security forces are counted as staff members.)

U&M may utilize the incinerator to dispose of trash bags.

Specialists may use testing equipment outside of testing permeters.

- Specialist Instructors+ are permitted to allow CIS Analysts to use testing equipment within a specialist event.

**There are more regulations regarding instance 294 in rule C1.**

_Until the Medical Department gets its equipment, they will be counted as scientists when doing medical tests._
_Veterinarian Program personnel may freely use vials for rehabilitation purposes._
cards.name: Rule E3 | Misusing Scientific Equipment

cards.desc:
Combatives should only ever decline escorting a test if they have a valid reason. Valid reasons for declining a test escort are as follows:

- The RsD requesting the test is an Assistant Researcher or if the MD requesting a checkup is below the rank of Nursing Student without a supervisor
- The TSCZ/CISCZ would not be properly secured without the combative in question (At least 2 security must remain inside TSCZ to guard)
- The only available combatives do not have the necessary tools to secure the test
- There is currently an identified CIS or breached specimen in the TSCZ or around it
- The situation in TSCZ is nearing a riot OR there are multiple problematic TS causing problems within the TSCZ
- There is currently an event in which SD personnel are partaking UNLESS said event involves testing
- There is an identified breached and confirmed hostile specimen somewhere in the CTZ
- There is an ongoing sitewide emergency i.e.: Breach, Raid, Riot, CTZ Lockdown, etc...

If a combative is seen denying test escorts for minuscule reasons, such as a personal grudge against the RsD in question, they will get infracted by EC. However, said combative may be given more leniency on that, provided they have a good reason which is not specified on this list. If the reason provided by the combative is seen as not fit, the combative will be infracted.
cards.name: Rule E3 | Combative Escort Procedures

cards.desc:
Due to the nature of site events and potential dangers encountered by testing, certain regulations are in place to assist the essential employees of the corporation in performing their events properly.

To help the process go smoothly and reduce the overall danger, a list of restricted actions for personnel accompanying the site event would be as follows:

- Personnel should stand at least 4 studs away from the windows in an observation room during an active test event.
- Personnel must refrain from opening or closing doors that have not been specifically instructed/allowed to open or close during an active test event unless it's required to participate in spectating the test. Opening the containment doors without special instruction during a test event, or afterward with present specimen or subjects inside, is strictly prohibited.
- Accompanying Personnel should not stand in between the subjects and the event host to avoid confusion in the subjects and so the event may be communicated clearly. Security personnel may freely do so for briefing and searching subjects. Security may also do so if the event host is being threatened by the subjects or if directed by the event host.
  - Spectators must not stand between the subjects and either the event host or security escort at any time unless it's required.
  - Spectators must not interrupt the event by attempting to speak to the subjects or being in the way of the event host while they are trying to communicate.
    - Being a general annoyance to the event host may result in your dismissal from spectating the event.

---

Personnel spectating any site event must ask for permission to do so from the event host unless the host states that anyone may freely spectate. The event host may also at any time dismiss you from spectating the event depending on departmental regulations that limit them or additional concerns from the host such as event interruption.

The following individuals may spectate freely unless found to violate any of the above-restricted actions or they are restricted by the security clearance required in special cases for Unit-4 testing:

- Administrative Staff
- ISB
- EC Board Agent+ (EC Board Member+ for Unit-4 tests)
- Supervisors to the event host

Failure to follow all instructions from the security escort or perform any of the listed restricted actions may result in your removal from the event.
cards.name: Rule E4 | Event Spectator Etiquette

cards.desc:
F1 infractions are almost if not always **added onto** original punishments as another infraction depending on the situation.
Exploiting loopholes within any rules will result in harsher punishment(s) depending on the rule broken.
Lying to intelligence personnel will make you liable for an F1 infraction;

- Lying in an attempt to incriminate an innocent person or to try and get out of your original punishment will result in a harsher verdict.
- Lying to intelligence to intervene with their duties will also make you liable for an F1 infraction.

Violators intentionally evading intelligence personnel while they are engaged in their official duties will be met with a F1 infraction on top of their original punishment. (Including but not limited to; leaving while being questioned, running from intel personnel, etc.)
cards.name: Rule F1 | Loopholes & Exploitations

cards.desc:
The attempt to or having another individual plan to perform a harmful action against other people (test subject or personnel) with malicious intent through means of:

- Hiring hitmen or setting bounties that grant rewards of any type.
  - An exemption is made for the SD Assignments board as well as the KOS orders from both SD and Maxiburger.
  - Maxiburger KOS orders can only be fulfilled within the Maxiburger establishment.
- Personnel planning to intentionally violate the CoE including when teamed on TS without authorization.
- Personnel planning on purposefully disrupting site events including when teamed on TS without authorization.
- Making serious threats against other personnel (i.e. threatening to terminate personnel in order to disrupt their duties).
- Using or publishing information from personnel only communication channels with the intent to aid hostile forces (i.e. streaming staff communications to users on Test Subject or otherwise hostile teams).

---

Personnel who are found performing any of the actions below are to be deemed as “going rogue” (referred to as a rogue). Suspected rogues may be apprehended by any personnel that can safely capture them and be reported to an Ethics Committee Agent as soon as possible:

- Personnel dropping or willfully giving access to equipment or tools to TS/CIS/CIV or otherwise hostile forces (this includes Maxiburger staff, despite them being a neutral force).
  - Putting departmentally issued tools/weapons, including decoy rifles, into green bins falls under this rule as a violation, they are to be placed in red bins.
- Personnel aiding or abetting TS/CIS/CIV, or otherwise hostile forces, with escaping or accessing unauthorized locations. This includes leaking site operations to hostile forces.
- Personnel breaking multiple Code of Ethics rules and/or breaking multiple sections of the same rule.
- Unauthorized personnel in possession of the Nuclear Authentication Disk (NAD) or Nuclear Access Key without any valid reason, or refusing to report discovery of/give it to L5+ Security Personnel.
- Personnel attempting to terminate multiple other personnel without proper justification.
- Personnel wearing disguises to break CoE and act as though they were a disguised Test Subject.
- Personnel causing mass site distress through means of the control room.
- Personnel intentionally infecting themselves while deployed on a departmental team through a puddle, a specimen chamber or by any other means. (The only exception to this is RAH hybridizing themselves, following their internal regulations)
- Personnel causing/planning an event to go wrong to instill chaos. (example: deliberate disregard for precaution letting armed, infected, or irradiated subjects run loose.)
- Any other action the Ethics Committee determines to be of significant damage to the corporation.
- Violating a **mandatory** suspension. See G2 for more information on mandatory suspensions.

Personnel determined to have gone rogue are to be punished with a global blacklist upon infraction and are to be logged in the Ethics Committee Roster:

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1p95f9DuNZg3LTULuYZ8AasUpdyh1Cc8Cg0IrdTemML4/edit?gid=1089969201#gid=1089969201](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1p95f9DuNZg3LTULuYZ8AasUpdyh1Cc8Cg0IrdTemML4/edit?gid=1089969201#gid=1089969201 "smartCard-inline")

People who have been found to go rogue on drafted personnel teams are only liable to being globally blacklisted if they otherwise hold a clearance. People who go rogue on drafted teams who do **not** hold clearance will be blacklisted from future draft events. (Also applies to standard infractions.)

(Note: In specific instances punishment may vary based on the consensus of EC)
cards.name: Rule F2 | Solicitation & Conspiracy

cards.desc: This will be about the warnings from the Ethics Committee for any warning(s), verbal or not, given to you. The EC member who wrote your infraction MUST inform you of the infraction and what you have been infracted for. Ethics personnel must have valid proof for your punishment or you may not be punished.
cards.name: G1 | Warnings Regulations

cards.desc:
In order for you to get your old infraction removed, you must request to see your infractions by an EC personnel by going into the Central Report Hub server and making an EC infraction expungement ticket. You must undergo a Voluntary Suspension to remove your infractions.

( [https://discord.gg/TAJgkwbCMK](https://discord.gg/TAJgkwbCMK "smartCard-inline")  )

The infraction may be removed if:

- The infraction does not have proof.
- The infraction is 1+ months old and is not unappealable.
- The infraction had no relevant proof.
- You did not receive an infraction during the past 30 days you are trying to expunge it in.

Note: B3 and appealable F2 & F1 voluntary suspensions are 48 and 168 hours respectively while all others able to expunged are 24 hours. If you have violated more than one CoE rule in one infraction, the expungement time will stack up, for example C1+A1 = 48 hour suspension.
Personnel may only expunge 1 infraction per week, and they may not have gained an infraction in the span of 1 month of the infraction that they are trying to expunge; in addition to this, you must hold at least an L1 clearance or be a LR+ within a GoI to be able to expunge an Infraction. (unless it’s an appealable GBL that you’re expunging)

---

**Regulations about Supervised Deployment:**

If you are undergoing a voluntary suspension to expunge an infraction then there is a system to allow you to still deploy on your department teams with certain restrictions. You must request to be supervised at all times while deployed by an EC member to monitor your behavior during the time of the voluntary suspension.

- EC Personnel can supervise both Combatants and Non-combatants.
- The one requesting a supervised deployment must do so ahead of time. EC personnel will meet them at either at EC spawn or their respective department spawn that the individual will deploy as.
- If the supervisor has been terminated by hostile forces or through other means of harm. The supervised personnel must head back to their spawn or EC spawn unless stated otherwise by the supervisor.
- If for any reason the supervisor has to leave, immediately swap to Facility Personnel or request for another supervisor to continue your supervised deployment. If none are available, then you must then swap to facility personnel until one is available.
- EC personnel may not supervise personnel who are on a mandatory suspension.

---

**Validity System**

This System will be used as a way to determine if the Supervised Deployment is a success or not.

- A warning is given when the personnel being supervised commits one of the acts listed in the warning section.
- If the personnel being supervised committed a CoE Violation during their supervision, the Supervisor will stop the supervision and infract the personnel. The voluntary suspension will be canceled and the timer will be reset on the ability to perform another expungement.
- Each warning must show evidence as to what caused them to receive it so that way the supervisor is accountable.
- If personnel receive more than 2 warnings or commit a CoE violation, the supervised deployment will be canceled the voluntary suspension will be canceled and the timer will be reset on the ability to perform another expungement.
- If the supervised deployment is successful and has been ongoing for a minimum of an hour, time from the initial suspension period may be removed with a ratio of 6 hours per 60 minutes supervised with a cap of 12 hours total.

---

**Warning Section**

This section lists possible actions that would count as a warning while under supervised deployment.

1. Faking a hit on someone with any melee weapon or needlessly swinging one.
2. Breaking any rule in the Code of Ethics
3. Straying away from the Supervisor without permission.
4. Unprofessional behavior or being a general annoyance to personnel on site through actions such as spamming the elevator button or throwing items at others
cards.name: G1 | Infraction Expungement

cards.desc:
#### **Infractions**

- First Infraction: First verbal warning.
- Second Infraction: First suspension which is 2 days.
- Third Infraction: Second suspension which is 4 days.
- Fourth Infraction: Third suspension which is 1 week.
- Fifth Infraction: Fourth suspension which is 2 weeks.
- Sixth Infraction: Exiled from department(s), may not rejoin until a week has passed.
  - Following the week, the user may **not** be reinstated into their department/rank. They are to re-do intake and rank up as if they are starting fresh.
- Seventh Infraction: Appealable blacklist after 6 weeks.
- Eighth Infraction: Unappealable blacklist.

[https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1p95f9DuNZg3LTULuYZ8AasUpdyh1Cc8Cg0IrdTemML4/view#gid=1089969201](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1p95f9DuNZg3LTULuYZ8AasUpdyh1Cc8Cg0IrdTemML4/view#gid=1089969201 "smartCard-inline")

Everything above is global and applies to all departments the violator is in.

The EC member who wrote your infraction MUST inform you of the infraction and what you have been infracted for. Ethics personnel must of had valid evidence at the time of posting for your punishment or you may not be punished.

Infractions that were valid at the time of posting are still considered valid even if the evidence expires or is no longer accessible.

Note: A2 infractions carry an additional minimum 1-week suspension in addition to the punishment for the infraction number given, it can range to an exile depending on severity (Example: Heavy sexual references, engagement in the aforementioned…).

---

#### **Warnings**

- Warnings are a reduced punishment if an infraction is deemed too severe for the offense.
- Warnings never expire and stay on record forever. EC members who issued your warning must inform you of it and what you're being warned for.
- Warnings cannot be issued for violations of the following sections:  **A2**, **F1**, **F2, and C3** (Only applies to the “Leaked Assets” section.) Violation of those sections is considered a serious offense.
- If you're a repeated offender (6+ warnings and/or 3+ _active_ infractions on record), the Ethics Committee reserves the right to issue an infraction, instead of a warning, even for minor violations.

---

### Appeals

You have the right to appeal your infraction if you think the verdict you have been given is wrong. If you wish to submit an appeal, you must open an infraction expungement ticket.

- You may appeal infractions at any time.
- You must provide all details regarding your infraction if possible.
- You must provide reasons as to why you believe your infraction should be appealed.

---

### Unappealable Infractions

An infraction will become entirely impossible to appeal if:

- It is an A2 infraction
- It is a severe enough F2 infraction. (ex: going rogue)
- If you have gained 4 infractions in two weeks or less, then all of those are considered unappealable.
- You have 8 or more active infractions in total.
- If you have violated your voluntary suspension terms without prior notice of withdrawing, then the infraction you were attempting to expunge will become unappealable for 30 days and will grant a G2 infraction as per the Suspension rules.
- You constantly appeal infractions and then continue stacking them up, or you have gained 4 infractions in four weeks or less. An Ethics Committee vote may be launched against you to deem your infractions unappealable.

---

### Suspensions

##### **Mandatory Suspensions**

These suspensions are given according to how many infractions one has. (This is outlines at the top of this section) While on this suspension, there are rules to deployment and are heavy punishments if it is violated;

- If you’re found to have violated a _mandatory_ suspension, your punishment will immediately rise to an exile from all departments and an **appealable global blacklist**.
- While on mandatory suspension, you **may NOT** have supervised deployment on departmental/GoI teams.
- While on mandatory suspension, you **may NOT** deploy on any teams (including Test Subject, Civilian, and CIS) EXCEPT for Facility personnel and Administrative Department.

##### **Voluntary Suspension**

These suspensions are given when one is attempting to expunge their infractions. However there are still rules for deploying even when the suspension is voluntary;

- While on voluntary suspension, you **may have** supervised deployment on departmental/GoI teams.
- While on voluntary suspension, you **may NOT** deploy on any teams (including Test Subject, Civilian, and CIS) EXCEPT for Facility personnel and Administrative Department UNLESS you have properly requested and are receiving proper supervision. (More information about this in G1)
- If you are found to be violating a _voluntary_ suspension it will make your infraction (that you were attempting to expunge) un-expungable for another 30 days and will also grant a G2 infraction.

---

#### **Zero Tolerance Policy**

A zero tolerance policy (ZTP) is a period of intensive scrutiny by the ethics committee where receiving an infraction or significant departmental punishment will result in you receiving a global blacklist. They can span from 1 week to 3 months long. They may be implemented for the following reasons:

- When appealing a blacklist.
- An Ethics Committee vote launched against you to place you on a ZTP.

---

#### **Global Blacklist**

A global blacklist (GBL) is a form of punishment that exiles you from all TSC departments, preventing you from rejoining any of them until it is appealed. You may find yourself on a global blacklist for the following reasons:

- You have 7 infractions (appealable), or 8+ infractions (unappealable).
- You have gone rogue (e.g.: shooting multiple staff members, running from EC/ISB constantly, and so on). This applies to all corporation teams.
- Found to be exploiting or otherwise violating serious ROBLOX ToS rules.
- Violating a mandatory suspension.

While globally blacklisted, there are certain rules that apply. This includes;

- You may not join the game on any department/division or personnel teams that have access to personnel equipment such as radios, wands, and anything not normally accessible by TS.
  - CIS is considered departmental, therefore globally blacklisted users may not join it.
  - Development teams follow their internal guidelines.
  - TSE and Maxiburger have the exception where their HiCOMM are allowed to decide whether or not a globally blacklisted user may join.
- Users who are a part of an External GoI and are Globally blacklisted, may not deploy at all.

cards.desc:
All personnel have at their disposal a handheld radio, which can be used to effectively communicate with other personnel at longer ranges and give out callouts for dangerous situations or anything in general.

Due to these portable radios being very valuable for communication, they have set rules when it come to using them, which can be found below.

When using radios, you are expected to follow all TSC and ToS rules, breaking them will warrant an infraction like normal.

Radios also have their own set of rules:

- You may not spam the radios with unnecessary messages
- You may not use the ping feature ( ex. \@‌everyone ) for unnecessary things. This is reserved for important messages only. How the ping feature works is if you very specifically type out a teams name, it makes your text yellow for them. Example: “ \@Recontainment Unit There is a breach in S2 “ would be yellow for RECON, allowing them to see it easier.
- You may not provide misinformation or lies on the radio, if you are unsure about something make sure to state so.

There are also certain channels available for certain departments. You may only use said channels for their designed purpose.

Combative channels are to speak about emergencies, callouts, site state, etc.

Staff channels are there to just communicate with eachother.

Global channel is a channel where you can speak about anything.

**IF THE RADIOS ARE BROKEN AND CHANNELS DON’T WORK PROPERLY, YOU MAY IGNORE THE PART ABOVE.**

cards.desc:
I’m gonna make this short and sweet, this is me quitting, forever! I actually like TSC so I won’t cause any damage but I’m putting this here for the people who need it. If you have the power to delete this Executive Order than please wait at least 24hrs so people can spread the word. This is my final request before I leave

---

If you’re struggling in real life or in TSC please rethink your stance in this game, like seriously, I’ve seen so many people including myself get worried and stressed over this game, some people even go to the brink of giving up over some stupid online community which you probably don’t even know or will know irl, most people in TSC only joined because they were bored or depressed, leading them to mindlessly rank up in a never ending cycle.
If you’re struggling mentally or physically focus on your real life instead of this game, it’s unhealthy and I can relate. Drop it when you can and stop investing so much time into it

Someone came to me a while ago really stressed out about this and another community, to the point they heavily blamed themselves for minor mistakes they made which me and them would have passed over in any other situation. I asked them if _they’re even having fun_ in this game and they couldn't answer, yet they still continued, this game is a trap and the only way to let yourself go is to understand why you’re here, why you need to leave, and to work on yourself in the real world instead of clocking onto some fake roblox cooperation

REAL LIFE IS MORE IMPORTANT

So please just leave if you’re struggling. Don’t hesitate like I did

---

If you’re some of the people who have a good balance of TSC and real life then please continue by all means, I do agree larping isn’t a great way to spend you time but it isn’t harmful by nature, the only reason it’s become bad is because of how much people play and why they play.

---

Also if you’re struggling with mental health don’t be afraid to let someone know, some people I trust a lot are EC command, if you DM them I can guarantee that you’ll be able to let some stress out. ISB can also be helpful but it depends who you ask, some people in there actually suck

Now. In case I don't see you, good morning, good afternoon and good night, o7 and god speed TSC
